Cleaning
After disassembly, all metal parts should be cleaned in
metal parts cleaner. Plastic parts and rubber parts should be
cleaned ONLY in alcohol. Care should be taken to prevent
chipping or cracking plastic parts. Replace all rubber parts,
except power diaphragms. After parts have been cleaned,
wash them thoroughly with alcohol and use clean, dry com­
pressed air to blow dirt and fluid out of recesses and internal
passages. Use all parts furnished in the repair kit.

### Inspection
`chevrolet_camaro_en_0f476a40` | camaro | pdf_manual | tier:3 | lang:en | layer:general | p:101

Inspect all parts for damage or excessive wear. The power
diaphragms must be free of kinks, cracks and tears. Replace
any damaged, worn or chipped parts.
Assembly
Be sure all parts are clean before assembling unit. Do not
let grease or mineral oil come in contact with any rubber
parts. Lubricate rubber parts of power piston group with
special lubricant included in service kit.

`chevrolet_camaro_en_e14f47a0` | camaro | pdf_manual | tier:3 | lang:en | layer:engine | p:103

The Single Diaphragm Hydrovac is a self contained
tional four-cycle gasoline engine (fig. ID). The Hydrovac
vacuum hydraulic power brake unit for use on a vehicle with
consists of three basic elements:
a vacuum source such as the intake manifold of the conven-

### The Hydrovac is attached to the vehicle frame by means
`chevrolet_camaro_en_05b08f7f` | camaro | pdf_manual | tier:3 | lang:en | layer:engine | p:104

of a mounting bracket attached to the power chamber shell
and a mounting pad boss on the side of the hydraulic cylin­
der. The vacuum inlet port of the vacuum control valve is
connected to the intake manifold or other vacuum source
through a vacuum check valve. The atmospheric port in the
control valve is connected to an air cleaner installed in a
location protected from road dirt and splash. The hydraulic
line from the brake master cylinder is attached to the fluid
inlet port on top of the Hydrovac hydraulic cylinder. The
outlet port of the Hydrovac is located in the end cap of the
hydraulic cylinder and is connected to the vehicle brake
wheel cylinders.

### CHEVROLET OVERHAUL MANUAL

BRAKES 5-30
Cleaning and Inspection
Thoroughly clean all metal parts in Bendix Metalclene or
equivalent. After cleaning, rewash all hydraulic system parts
in clean isopropyl alcohol or equivalent before reassembly.
Inspect all parts for excessive wear or damage. Replace worn
or damaged parts. Inspect control valve body atmospheric
valve seat. If damaged, replace housing. Always use the cor­
rect repair kit when overhauling unit.

1.
To install a new push rod seal (13) in push rod (8), place
new seal (Rubber side down) on a clean block of wood.
2.
Hold push rod vertically (threaded end up) with drilled
end of rod resting on shaft end of seal and then strike
threaded end of push rod with soft hammer to seat seal
with its shoulder firmly against end of push rod.

### Dip cup (9) in brake fluid and assemble cup on piston

( 10) with lip of cup as shown.

Install piston parts (2 through 12) on push rod from
seal end of push rod in order shown.
5.
Slide snap ring (7), stop washer (6), bearing (4) with

cup (3), seal retainer (2), retainer ring (12) and piston
assembly ( 1) on push rod.

`chevrolet_camaro_en_b9b4786e` | camaro | pdf_manual | tier:3 | lang:en | layer:engine | p:106

rod. Secure pin in place with retainer ring (12), making
certain ring is seated in groove on piston.

back to back. Then assemble piston, washer (6) and
diaphragm (7) and seat inner bead of diaphragm in
piston groove.
2.

### Lay piston and diaphragm assembly aside. Assemble
`chevrolet_camaro_en_99e0d71e` | camaro | pdf_manual | tier:3 | lang:en | layer:body | p:106

poppet return spring ( 11), vacuum poppet ( 10) and at­

stem. (Set valve body with vacuum poppet down on 1"
wooden cube and tap retainer with soft hammer until
it snaps onto stem of vacuum poppet).

### Assemble cover (16) securely in groove of valve body.

der bore. Secure valve body with four capscrews (13).

### Tighten screws to 40-60 in. lbs. Install check valve (A),

(Fig. 2D)

2.
Align scribe marks on both shells. Make certain bead
of diaphragm is seated in outer flanges of both shells
and hold rear shell in position while assembling clamp
band (8) over flanges of shells and bead of diaphragm.

### Position opening in band 45 degrees off vertical center
`chevrolet_camaro_en_ef8f97e4` | camaro | pdf_manual | tier:3 | lang:en | layer:interior | p:106

line of Hydrovac on side away from mounting bracket.
3.
Squeeze ends of band together and assemble bolt (9)
and nut (7). Tap band lightly with soft hammer while
tightening bolt to seat band securely on shells. After
tapping, re-tighten to 40-60 in. lbs.
4.

### Place new seal (2) on control tube (3), as shown, and
`chevrolet_camaro_en_c857c91b` | camaro | pdf_manual | tier:3 | lang:en | layer:brakes | p:106

assemble hose (4) to tube (5) of rear shell and to control
tube. Attach tube and nut (3) to control valve body
port. Securely tighten to 7-10 ft. lbs.

SUBJECT

### INTRODUCTION
`chevrolet_camaro_en_9e85bf44` | camaro | pdf_manual | tier:3 | lang:en | layer:engine | p:109

This section, convering all gasoline engines, has been
condensed using only typical illustrations and procedures
(except where specific illustrations and procedures will help
clarify the operation). The similatity of engines, engine parts
and engine sub-assemblies and the resulting similarity of
procedures required to service these units should aid the
technician in servicing the many engines.

### Many operations outlined in this section, when done as
`chevrolet_camaro_en_709ada88` | camaro | pdf_manual | tier:3 | lang:en | layer:engine | p:109

single operations and not part of a general overhaul, should
be performed with the engine in the vehicle.
In order to avoid repetition and to identify the engines
involved in a particular procedure, the 307-, 3 50-, and 400cu. in. V8 engines are identified as "Small V8’s". The 402and 454cu. in. V8 engines are identified as "Mark IV V8’s".

### CHEVROLET OVERHAUL MANUAL
`chevrolet_camaro_en_88cedb7a` | camaro | pdf_manual | tier:3 | lang:en | layer:engine | p:109

ENGINE 6-2
GENERAL DESCRIPTION
IN-LINE ENGINES
Cylinders are numbered front to rear. Firing order is
1-5-36-2-4 for the L6 engines. Crankshaft rotation as viewed
from the rear is counter-clockwise.
The L6 crankshaft has seven main bearings and the cam­
shaft has four bearings.
Full pressure lubrication, through a full flow oil filter is
furnished by a gear-type oil pump. The distributor, driven by
a helical gear on the camshaft, drives the oil pump. The main
oil gallery feeds oil, through drilled passages, to the camshaft
and crankshaft to lubricate the bearings. The main oil gallery
also feeds the valve lifters which, through hollow push rods,
feed the individually mounted rocker arms (fig. 1).

### V8 ENGINES
`chevrolet_camaro_en_8ea22e22` | camaro | pdf_manual | tier:3 | lang:en | layer:engine | p:110

Cylinders are numbered front to rear, 1-3-5-7 on the left
bank and 2-4-6-8 on the right bank. Firing order is, 1-84-3-6-5-7-2. Crankshaft rotation as viewed from the rear is
counter-clockwise.
The crankshaft has five main bearings and the camshaft
has five bearings.
Full pressure lubrication through a full flow oil filter, is
furnished by a gear-type oil pump. The distributor, driven by
a helical gear on the camshaft, drives the oil pump. The main
oil gallery feeds oil, through drilled passages, to the camshaft
and crankshaft to lubricate the bearings. The valve lifter oil
gallery feeds the valve lifters which, through hollow push
rods, feed the individually mounted rocker arms (fig. 2 and
3).

a.

### On engines using a STEEL gasket, coat both sides
`chevrolet_camaro_en_46fe8e8b` | camaro | pdf_manual | tier:3 | lang:en | layer:general | p:117

of gasket with sealer, spread the sealer thin and
even. Too much sealer may hold the beads of the
gasket away from the head or block. One method of
applying the sealer that will assure the proper coat
is with the use of a paint roller.

### CAUTION: Use no sealer on engines using a compo­
`chevrolet_camaro_en_5e35c4a9` | camaro | pdf_manual | tier:3 | lang:en | layer:engine | p:117

sition STEEL ASBESTOS gasket.
b.
Place the gasket in position over the dowel pins,
with the bead up.
c.
Carefully guide cylinder head into place over dowel
pins and gasket.
d.
Coat threads of cylinder head bolts with sealing
compound and install finger tight.
e.

### Tighten cylinder head bolts a little at a time in
`chevrolet_camaro_en_a3ff0a50` | camaro | pdf_manual | tier:3 | lang:en | layer:engine | p:117

torque sequence shown in Figure 77 until the speci­
fied torque is reached. (See Engine Torques.)
NOTE: All engines using composition STEEL ASBESTOS
gaskets must have the cylinder head retorqued
after engine warm-up.
10.

### Install valve lifters and push rods. Install in the same
`chevrolet_camaro_en_56323d3f` | camaro | pdf_manual | tier:3 | lang:en | layer:engine | p:117

location from which removed during engine disassem­
bly.
NOTE: Whenever new valve lifters and/or rocker
arms and balls are being installed coat foot of valve
lifters and surfaces of rocker arms and balls with
“ MOLYKOTE”or its equivalent.
11.

### Install valve rocker arm s, rocker arm balls and
`chevrolet_camaro_en_5405cb00` | camaro | pdf_manual | tier:3 | lang:en | layer:engine | p:117

nuts and tighten rocker arm  nuts until all push
ro d  end play is taken up.
12.
On In-Line engines, install push rod covers.
13.
Install intake and exhaust manifolds. Torque to specifi­
cations in the sequence outlined under "Torque Specifi­
cations" Figure 77.
14.

### Install the following sub-assemblies (if applicable) as
`chevrolet_camaro_en_27048e2c` | camaro | pdf_manual | tier:3 | lang:en | layer:engine | p:117

outlined in the applicable "Chassis Service Manual".
•  Oil Dip Stick Tube and Oil Dip Stick
•  Ground Strap
•  Clutch Pressure Plate and Disc
•  Starter
•  Oil Filter (new)
•  Carburetor and Fuel Lines
•  Distributor Cap (with spark plug wires)
•  Fuel Pump (and fuel pump push rod on V8
engines)
•  W ater Pump (and by pass hose)
•  Accessory Drive Pulley(s) (and belts)
•  Delcotron (with brackets)
•  Air Injection Reactor System (with brackets)
15.

### Adjust all belts as necessary.
`chevrolet_camaro_en_88e1738b` | camaro | pdf_manual | tier:3 | lang:en | layer:engine | p:117

16.
Adjust valves as outlined under Valve Mechanism, In­
stallation and Adjustment in the applicable "Chassis
Service Manual".
17.
Attach engine lift at appropriate cylinder head bolt
location or at engine lift brackets.

### CYLINDER HEAD ASSEM BLIES

Disassembly
1.
With cylinder head removed, remove valve rocker arm
nuts, balls and rocker arms (if not previously done).
2.
Using Tool J-8062, compress the valve springs (fig. 13)
and remove valve keys. Release the compressor tool and
remove spring caps, spring shields (if so equipped)
springs and spring damper, then remove oil seals and
valve spring shims.

### Cleaning
`chevrolet_camaro_en_10811373` | camaro | pdf_manual | tier:3 | lang:en | layer:general | p:118

1.
Clean all carbon from combustion chambers and valve
ports using Tool J-8089 (fig. 14).
2.
Thoroughly clean the valve guides using Tool J-8101
(fig15).
3.
Clean all carbon and sludge from push rods, rocker
arms and push rod guides.
4.

### Clean valve stems and heads on a buffing wheel.
`chevrolet_camaro_en_e964d44d` | camaro | pdf_manual | tier:3 | lang:en | layer:engine | p:118

5.
Clean carbon deposits from head gasket mating surface.
Inspection
1.
Inspect the cylinder head for cracks in the exhaust
ports, combustion chambers, or external cracks to the
water chamber.
2.
Inspect the valves for burned heads, cracked faces or
damaged stems.

### NOTE: Excessive valve stem to bore clearance will
`chevrolet_camaro_en_5e9c65fa` | camaro | pdf_manual | tier:3 | lang:en | layer:engine | p:118

cause excessive oil consumption and may cause
valve breakage. Insufficient clearance will result in
noisy and sticky functioning of the valve and disturb
engine smoothness.
Measure valve stem clearance (fig. 16) as follows:

### Clamp a dial indicator on one side of the cylinder head
`chevrolet_camaro_en_c69d02ed` | camaro | pdf_manual | tier:3 | lang:en | layer:interior | p:118

rocker arm cover gasket rail, locating the indicator so
that movement of the valve stem from side to side
(crosswise to the head) will cause a direct movement of
the indicator stem. The indicator stem must contact the
side of the valve stem just above the valve guide. With
the valve head dropped about 1/16" off the valve seat;
move the stem of the valve from side to side using light
pressure to obtain a clearance reading. If clearance ex­
ceeds specifications it will be necessary to ream valve
guides for oversize valves as outlined.

`chevrolet_camaro_en_067cfd5c` | camaro | pdf_manual | tier:3 | lang:en | layer:engine | p:119

fied height and checked against the specifications

### VALVE SEATS
`chevrolet_camaro_en_7d708fbc` | camaro | pdf_manual | tier:3 | lang:en | layer:engine | p:120

Reconditioning the valve seats is very important, because
the seating of the valves must be perfect for the engine to
deliver the power and performance built into it.
Another important factor is the cooling of the valve heads.

### Good contact between each valve and its seat in the head is
`chevrolet_camaro_en_572a2b57` | camaro | pdf_manual | tier:3 | lang:en | layer:interior | p:120

imperative to insure that the heat in the valve head will be
properly carried away.
Several different types of equipment are available for re­
seating valves seats. The recommendations of the manufac­
turer of the equipment being used should be carefully
followed to attain proper results.

### Regardless of what type of equipment is used, however, it
`chevrolet_camaro_en_37fbc8b1` | camaro | pdf_manual | tier:3 | lang:en | layer:general | p:120

is essential that valve guide bores be free from carbon or dirt
3.
to insure proper centering of pilot in the guide.
Fig. 2 1 -ln sta llin g  Rocker A rm  Stud (In-Line and “ Small V 8 ” )
Install expanding pilot in the valve guide bore and ex­
pand pilot.

### Place roughing stone or forming stone over pilot and
`chevrolet_camaro_en_4a62e2ec` | camaro | pdf_manual | tier:3 | lang:en | layer:interior | p:120

just clean up the valve seat. Use a stone cut to specifica­
tions.
Remove roughing stone or forming stone from pilot,
place finishing stone, cut to specifications, over pilot
and cut just enough metal from the seat to provide a
smooth finish. Refer to specifications and Figure 23.

### Narrow down the valve seat to the specified width.
`chevrolet_camaro_en_8d667b2a` | camaro | pdf_manual | tier:3 | lang:en | layer:engine | p:120

NOTE: This operation is done by grinding the port
side with a 30 degree stone to lower seat and a 60
degree stone to raise seat.
Remove expanding pilot and clean cylinder head care­
fully to remove all chips and grindings from above oper­
ations.

### Measure valve seat concentricity (fig. 24).

VALVES
wear, or valves that are warped excessively should be re­
placed. When a valve head which is warped excessively is
refaced, a knife edge will be ground on part or all of the valve
head due to the amount of metal that must be removed to
completely reface. Knife edges lead to breakage, burning or
pre-ignition due to heat localizing on this knife edge. If the
edge of the valve head is less than 1/32" thick after grinding,
replace the valve.

### Several different types of equipment are available for
`chevrolet_camaro_en_5af9c297` | camaro | pdf_manual | tier:3 | lang:en | layer:general | p:121

refacing valves. The recommendations of the manufacturer
of the equipment being used should be carefully followed to
attain proper results.
1.
If necessary, dress the valve refacing machine grinding
wheel to make sure it is smooth and true. Set chuck at
angle specified for valve. Refer to specifications and

### Figure 23.
`chevrolet_camaro_en_e6e09b0a` | camaro | pdf_manual | tier:3 | lang:en | layer:lighting | p:121

2.
Clamp the valve stem in the chuck of the machine.
3.
Start the grinder and move the valve head in line with
the grinder wheel.
4.
Turn the feed screw until the valve head just contacts
wheel. Move valve back and forth across the wheel and
regulate the feed screw to provide light valve contact.
5.

### Continue grinding until the valve face is true and
`chevrolet_camaro_en_06e477ea` | camaro | pdf_manual | tier:3 | lang:en | layer:general | p:121

smooth all around the valve. If this makes the valve
head thin (1/32" min.) the valve must be replaced as the
valve will overheat and burn.
6.
Remove valve from chuck and place stem in "V" block.
Feed valve squarely against grinding wheel to grind any
pit from rocker arm end of stem.

### Fig. 24-M easuring Valve Seat Concentricity
`chevrolet_camaro_en_eebd55de` | camaro | pdf_manual | tier:3 | lang:en | layer:general | p:121

Valves that are pitted can be refaced to the proper angle,
insuring correct relation between the head and stem on a
valve refacing mechanism. Valve stems which show excessive
NOTE: Only the extreme end of the valve stem is
hardened to resist wear. Do not grind end of stem
excessively.

### ENGINE 6-14
`chevrolet_camaro_en_6f6d6145` | camaro | pdf_manual | tier:3 | lang:en | layer:engine | p:122

7.
After cleaning valve face and cylinder head valve seat
of grinding particles, make pencil marks about 1/4"
apart across the valve face, place the valve in cylinder
head and give the valve 1/2 turn in each direction while
exerting firm pressure on head of valve.
8.

### Remove valve and check face carefully. If all pencil
`chevrolet_camaro_en_6f08184a` | camaro | pdf_manual | tier:3 | lang:en | layer:interior | p:122

marks have not been removed at the point of contact
with the valve seat, it will be necessary to repeat the
refacing operation and again recheck for proper seating.
9.
Grind and check the remaining valves in the same man­
ner.

### Assembly
`chevrolet_camaro_en_74133472` | camaro | pdf_manual | tier:3 | lang:en | layer:general | p:122

1.
Insert a valve in the proper port.
2.
Assemble the valve spring and related parts as follows:
IN-LINE AND "SMALL V8"
a.
Set the valve spring shim, valve spring (with damper
if used), valve shield and valve cap or rotator in
place (fig. 25).
b.

### Compress the spring with Tool J-8062.
`chevrolet_camaro_en_df96a8a3` | camaro | pdf_manual | tier:3 | lang:en | layer:interior | p:122

c.
Install oil seal in the lower groove of the stem, mak­
ing sure that the seal is flat and not twisted.
d.
Install the valve locks and release the compressor
tool, making sure that the locks seat properly in the
upper groove of the valve stem.

### M A R K IV V8
`chevrolet_camaro_en_28502653` | camaro | pdf_manual | tier:3 | lang:en | layer:interior | p:122

a.
Install valve spring shim on valve
spring seat then install a new valve stem oil seal over
valve and valve guide.
b.
Set the valve spring (with damper), and valve cap in
place (fig. 26).
Fig. 26--Exhaust Valve Spring Installation (“ Mark IV V 8 ” )
c.

### Compress the spring with Tool J-8062.
`chevrolet_camaro_en_a350289d` | camaro | pdf_manual | tier:3 | lang:en | layer:interior | p:122

d.
Install the valve locks and release the compressor
tool, making sure the locks seat properly in the
groove of the valve stem.
NOTE: Grease may be used to hold the locks in
place, while releasing the compressor tool.
3.

### Install the remaining valves.
`chevrolet_camaro_en_db71f6dc` | camaro | pdf_manual | tier:3 | lang:en | layer:engine | p:122

4.
On In-Line and "Small V8" engines check each
valve stem oil seal by placing a vacuum cup or
similar device over the end of the valve stem and
against the cap. Operate the vacuum cup and make
sure no air leaks past the seal. A vacuum cup can
be made from a small syringe and a high voltage
shield (fig. 27).
5.

### Check the installed height of the valve springs, using a
`chevrolet_camaro_en_e2996f0c` | camaro | pdf_manual | tier:3 | lang:en | layer:interior | p:122

narrow thin scale. A cutaway scale will help (fig. 28).
Measure from the top of the shim or the spring seat to
the top of the valve spring or valve spring shield (fig.
29). If this is found to exceed the specified height, install
a valve spring seat shim approximately 1/16" thick. At
no time should the spring be shimmed to give an in­
stalled height under the minimum specified.

VALVE LIFTERS (HYDRAULIC)
Two types of hydraulic lifters are used. Both types of
lifters operate on the same principle and are serviced basi­
cally in the same manner. The complete lifter assemblies are
interchangeable but parts from one lifter are not interchange­
able with another. Both lifters are easily identified by the
outside configuration of the lifter body. For purposes of iden­
tification we refer to them as lifter "A" and lifter "B" (fig.
30).

`chevrolet_camaro_en_f134c5a1` | camaro | pdf_manual | tier:3 | lang:en | layer:interior | p:123

the blade of a small screw driver, remove the push
rod seat retainer.
2.
Remove the push rod seat and metering valve (lifter
"A") or the push rod seat and inertia valve assembly
(lifter "B") (fig. 30).
3.

### Remove the plunger, ball check valve assembly and
`chevrolet_camaro_en_c890e498` | camaro | pdf_manual | tier:3 | lang:en | layer:general | p:123

the plunger spring.
4.
Remove the ball check valve and spring by prying
the ball retainer loose from the plunger with the
blade of a small screw driver (fig. 31).

Cleaning and Inspection
Thoroughly clean all parts in cleaning solvent, and inspect
them carefully. If any parts are damaged or worn the entire
lifter assembly should be replaced. If the lifter body wall is
scuffed or worn, inspect the cylinder block lifter bore, if the
bottom of the lifter is scuffed or worn inspect the camshaft
lobe, if the push rod seat is scuffed or worn inspect the push
rod.

### NOTE: Inertia valve and retainer (lifter “ B” ) (fig. 30)
`chevrolet_camaro_en_676d1859` | camaro | pdf_manual | tier:3 | lang:en | layer:interior | p:124

should not be removed from the push rod seat. To
check the valve, shake the push rod seat and inertia
valve assembly and the valve should move.

### VALVE LIFTERS (MECHANICAL)
`chevrolet_camaro_en_0e2eb921` | camaro | pdf_manual | tier:3 | lang:en | layer:engine | p:125

Cleaning and Inspection
The mechanical valve lifter (fig. 34) should never be disas­
sembled. Wash lifter assembly in cleaning solvent and dry
with compressed air. Blow out oil holes in lifter body and
push rod seat with compressed air. Inspect push rod seat
retainer. Inspect lifter for scuffed or worn lifter body or push
rod seat. If the lifter body wall is scuffed or worn inspect the
cylinder block lifter bore. If the bottom of the lifter is scuffed
or worn inspect the camshaft lobe, if the push rod seat is
scuffed or worn inspect the push rod. Additive containing EP
lube such as EOS should always be added to crankcase oil for
run-in when any new camshaft or lifters are installed. All
damaged or worn lifters should be replaced.

### Fig. 34-M echanical Valve Lifter
`chevrolet_camaro_en_2897033a` | camaro | pdf_manual | tier:3 | lang:en | layer:general | p:125

NOTE: Before installing lifter, coat the bottom of
the lifter w ith“ Molykote” or its equivalent.
OIL PUMP
The oil pump consists of two gears and a pressure regula­
tor valve enclosed in a two-piece housing. The oil pump is
driven by the distributor shaft which is driven by a helical
gear on the camshaft.

### A baffle is incorporated on the pickup screen to eliminate
`chevrolet_camaro_en_9bf4673c` | camaro | pdf_manual | tier:3 | lang:en | layer:engine | p:125

pressure loss due to sudden surging stops.

MAIN BEARINGS
Main bearings are of the precision insert type and do not
utilize shim for adjustment. If clearances are found to be
excessive a new bearing, both upper and lower halves will be
required. Bearings are available in standard size and .001",
.002", .009", .010",.020" and .030" undersize.

### Selective fitting of both rod and main bearing inserts is
`chevrolet_camaro_en_6cf3f779` | camaro | pdf_manual | tier:3 | lang:en | layer:general | p:127

necessary in production in order to obtain close tolerances.
For this reason you may find one half of a standard insert
with one half of a .001" undersize insert which will decrease
the clearance .0005" from using a full standard bearing.

### When a production crankshaft cannot be precision fitted
`chevrolet_camaro_en_420b84f6` | camaro | pdf_manual | tier:3 | lang:en | layer:engine | p:127

by this method, it is then ground .009" undersize on main
journals only. A .009"undersize bearing and .OIO"undersize bear­
ing may be used for percision fitting in the same manner as
previously described. Any engine fitted with a .009"undersize
crankshaft will be identified by the following markings.
•  “ .009” will be stam ped on the crankshaft counter­
w eight forw ard of the center m ain journal.
•  A figure “9” will be stam ped on the block at the left
front oil pan rail.

### NOTE: If, for any reason, main bearing caps are
`chevrolet_camaro_en_74a8e255` | camaro | pdf_manual | tier:3 | lang:en | layer:general | p:127

replaced, shimming may be necessary. Laminated
shims for each cap are available for service. Shim
requirement will be determined by bearing clear­
ance.
Inspection
In general, the lower half of the bearing (except No. 1
bearing) shows a greater wear and the most distress from
fatigue. If upon inspection the lower half is suitable for use,
it can be assumed that the upper half is also satisfactory. If
the lower half shows evidence of wear or damage, both upper
and lower halves should be replaced. Never replace one half
without replacing the other half.

### Checking Clearance
`chevrolet_camaro_en_24e89f6c` | camaro | pdf_manual | tier:3 | lang:en | layer:engine | p:127

To obtain the most accurate results with "Plastigage", (or
its equivalent) a wax-like plastic material which will com­
press evenly between the bearing and journal surfaces with­
out damaging either surface, certain precautions should be
observed. If the engine is out of the vehicle and upside down,
the crankshaft will rest on the upper bearings and the total
clearance can be measured between the lower bearing and
journal. If the engine is to remain in the vehicle, the crank­
shaft should be supported both front and rear (damper and
flywheel) to remove the clearance from the upper bearing.

### The total clearance can then be measured between the lower
`chevrolet_camaro_en_7b90fafe` | camaro | pdf_manual | tier:3 | lang:en | layer:interior | p:127

bearing and journal.
NOTE: To assure the proper seating of the crank­
shaft all bearing cap bolts should be at their speci­
fied torque. In addition, preparatory to checking fit
of bearings, the surface of the crankshaft journal
and bearing should be wiped clean of oil.
1.

### With the oil pan and oil pump removed, and starting
`chevrolet_camaro_en_5a2b608f` | camaro | pdf_manual | tier:3 | lang:en | layer:general | p:127

with the rear main bearing, remove bearing cap and
wipe oil from journal and bearing cap.
2.
Place a piece of gauging plastic the full width of the
bearing (parallel to the crankshaft) on the journal (fig.
40).

### Fig. 40~Gauging Plastic on Journal
`chevrolet_camaro_en_ac5d7742` | camaro | pdf_manual | tier:3 | lang:en | layer:engine | p:127

CHEVROLET OVERHAUL MANUAL
ENGINE 6-20
CAUTION: Do not rotate the crankshaft while the
gauging plastic is between the bearing and journal.
3.
Install the bearing cap and evenly torque the retaining
bolts to specifications.
4.

### Remove bearing cap. The flattened gauging plastic will
`chevrolet_camaro_en_b7e7ec9d` | camaro | pdf_manual | tier:3 | lang:en | layer:general | p:128

be found adhering to either the bearing shell or journal.
5.
On the edge of gauging plastic envelope there is a gra­
duated scale which is correlated in thousandths of an
inch. W ithout removing the gauging plastic, measure its
compressed width (at the widest point) with the gradua­
tions on the gauging plastic envelope (fig. 41).

### NOTE: Normally, main bearing journals wear evenly
`chevrolet_camaro_en_56350063` | camaro | pdf_manual | tier:3 | lang:en | layer:general | p:128

and are not out-ofround. However, if a bearing is
being fitted to an out-of-round journal (.001 ' max.), be
sure to fit to the maximum diameter of the journal:
If the bearing is fitted to the minimum diameter and
the journal is out-of-round .001',' interference be­
tween the bearing and journal will result in rapid
bearing failure. If the flattened gauging plastic ta­
pers toward the middle or ends, there is a difference
in clearance indicating taper, low spot or other ir­
regularity of the bearing or journal. Be sure to meas­
ure the journal with a micrometer if the flattened
gauging plastic indicates more than .001 'difference.
6.

### If the bearing clearance is within specifications, the
`chevrolet_camaro_en_c8ecda7c` | camaro | pdf_manual | tier:3 | lang:en | layer:general | p:128

bearing insert is satisfactory. If the clearance is not
within specifications, replace the insert. Always replace
both upper and lower insert as a unit.
Fig. 41-M easuring Gauging Plastic
NOTE: If a new bearing cap is being installed and
clearance is less than .001'' inspect for burrs or
nicks; if none are found then install shims as re­
quired.
7.

### A standard, .001" or .002" undersize bearing may pro­
`chevrolet_camaro_en_7905a03f` | camaro | pdf_manual | tier:3 | lang:en | layer:general | p:128

duce the proper clearance. If not, it will be necessary to
regrind the crankshaft journal for use with the next
undersize bearing.
8.
Proceed to the next bearing. After all bearings have
been checked rotate the crankshaft to see that there is
no excessive drag.
9.

### Measure crankshaft end play (see specifications) by
`chevrolet_camaro_en_e0528592` | camaro | pdf_manual | tier:3 | lang:en | layer:engine | p:128

forcing the crankshaft to the extreme front position.
Measure at the front end of the rear main bearing with
a feeler guage (fig. 42).
10.
Install a new rear main bearing oil seal in the cylinder
block and main bearing cap.

Connecting rod bearings are of the precision insert type
and do not utilize shims for adjustment. DO NOT FILE

### Cleaning and Inspection
`chevrolet_camaro_en_94ab6ac2` | camaro | pdf_manual | tier:3 | lang:en | layer:general | p:132

CONNECTING RODS
Wash connecting rods in cleaning solvent and dry with
compressed air.
Check for twisted or bent rods and inspect for nicks or
cracks. Replace connecting rods that are damaged.
PISTONS
Clean varnish from piston skirts and pins with a cleaning
solvent. DO NOT W IRE BRUSH ANY PART OF THE

### PISTON. Clean the ring grooves with a groove cleaner and
`chevrolet_camaro_en_616d45d3` | camaro | pdf_manual | tier:3 | lang:en | layer:general | p:132

make sure oil ring holes and slots are clean.
Inspect the piston for cracked ring lands, skirts or pin
bosses, wavy or worn ring lands, scuffed or damaged skirts,
eroded areas at top of the piston. Replace pistons that are
damaged or show signs of excessive wear.

### Inspect the grooves for nicks or burrs that might cause the
`chevrolet_camaro_en_cccf23c1` | camaro | pdf_manual | tier:3 | lang:en | layer:engine | p:132

rings to hang up.
Measure piston skirt (across center line of piston pin) and
check clearance as outlined under "Piston Selection".
PISTON PINS
The piston pin clearance is designed to maintain adequate
clearance under all engine operating conditions. Because of
this, the piston and piston pin are a matched set and not
serviced separately.

### Inspect piston pin bores and piston pins for wear. Piston
`chevrolet_camaro_en_7c06526b` | camaro | pdf_manual | tier:3 | lang:en | layer:general | p:132

pin bores and piston pins must be free of varnish or scuffing
when being measured. The piston pin should be measured
with a micrometer and the piston pin bore should be mea­
sured with a dial bore gauge or an inside micrometer. If
clearance is in excess of the .001" wear limit, the piston and
piston pin assembly should be replaced.

All compression rings are marked on the upper side of the
ring. When installing compression rings, make sure the
marked side is toward the top of the piston. The top ring is
chrome faced, or treated with molybdenum for maximum
life.

d.
Flex the oil ring assembly to make sure ring is free.
If binding occurs at any point the cause should be
determined, and if caused by ring groove, remove by
dressing groove with a fine cut file. If binding is
caused by a distorted ring, check a new ring.
e.

### Install second compression ring expander then ring
`chevrolet_camaro_en_ec5eabd3` | camaro | pdf_manual | tier:3 | lang:en | layer:general | p:133

with gaps properly located.
f.
Install top compression ring with gap properly
located.
9.
Proper clearance of the piston ring in its piston ring
groove is very important to provide proper ring action
and reduce wear. Therefore, when fitting new rings, the
clearances between the surfaces of the ring and groove
should be measured (fig. 59). (See Specifications.)

### Check crankshaft for run-out by supporting at the front

CAM SHAFT
Inspection
The camshaft bearing journals should be measured with
a micrometer for an out-of-round condition. If the journals
exceed .001" out-of-round, the camshaft should be replaced.

### The camshaft should also be checked for alignment. The
`chevrolet_camaro_en_94971868` | camaro | pdf_manual | tier:3 | lang:en | layer:general | p:137

best method is by use of "V" blocks and a dial indicator (fig.
64). The dial indicator will indicate the exact amount the
camshaft is out of true. If it is out more than .0015" dial
indicator reading, the camshaft should be replaced.

### O n In-L ine engines inspect the cam shaft gear and
`chevrolet_camaro_en_4e069ee7` | camaro | pdf_manual | tier:3 | lang:en | layer:general | p:137

thrust plate for wear or dam age. M easure the cam shaft
end play. This should be .001" to .005" (fig. 65).
Oil Nozzle Replacement (In Line)
1.
Remove nozzle with pliers (fig. 66).
2.
Drive new nozzle in place (oil hole in vertical position)
using a suitable light plastic or rubber hammer.

`chevrolet_camaro_en_6cfdf784` | camaro | pdf_manual | tier:3 | lang:en | layer:engine | p:137

of remover on table of a press and press shaft out of gear
(fig. 67).

Inspection

### Removal
`chevrolet_camaro_en_62975932` | camaro | pdf_manual | tier:3 | lang:en | layer:engine | p:140

Camshaft bearings can be replaced while engine is disas­
sembled for overhaul, or without complete disassembly of the
engine. To replace bearings without complete disassembly
remove the camshaft and crankshaft leaving cylinder heads
attached and pistons in place. Before removing crankshaft,
tape threads of connecting rod bolts to prevent damage to
crankshaft. Fasten connecting rods against sides of engine so
they will not be in the way while replacing camshaft bearings.
1.

### With camshaft and crankshaft removed, drive camshaft
`chevrolet_camaro_en_01de5d49` | camaro | pdf_manual | tier:3 | lang:en | layer:engine | p:140

rear plug from cylinder block.
NOTE: This procedure is based on removal of the
bearings nearest center of the engine first. With this
method a minimum amount of turns are necessary
to remove all bearings.
2.

### Using Tool Set J-6098, with nut and thrust washer
`chevrolet_camaro_en_01b0d452` | camaro | pdf_manual | tier:3 | lang:en | layer:general | p:140

installed to end of threads, index pilot in camshaft front
bearing and install puller screw through pilot.
3.
Install remover and installer tool with shoulder toward
bearing, making sure a sufficient amount of threads are
engaged.
4.

### Using two wrenches, hold puller screw while turning
`chevrolet_camaro_en_c22ccc95` | camaro | pdf_manual | tier:3 | lang:en | layer:general | p:140

nut. When bearing has been pulled from bore, remove
remover and installer tool and bearing from Duller
screw (fig. 68).
*
5.
Rem ove rem aining bearings (except front and rear)
in the sam e m anner. It will be necessary to index
pilot in cam shaft rear bearing to rem ove the rear
interm ediate bearing.
6.

### A ssem ble rem over and installer tool on driver
`chevrolet_camaro_en_6e12bb8a` | camaro | pdf_manual | tier:3 | lang:en | layer:engine | p:140

handle and rem ove cam shaft front and rear b ear­
ings by driving tow ards center o f cylinder block
(fig. 67).
Installation
The camshaft front and rear bearings should be installed
first. These bearings will act as guides for the pilot and center
the remaining bearings being pulled into place.
1.

### Assemble remover and installer tool on driver handle
`chevrolet_camaro_en_f69b7d54` | camaro | pdf_manual | tier:3 | lang:en | layer:engine | p:140

and install camshaft front and rear bearings by driving
towards center of cylinder block (fig. 69).
Fig. 68--Replacing Camshaft Center Bearing
2.
Using Tool Set J-6098, with nut then thrust washer
installed to end of threads, index pilot in camshaft front
bearing and install puller screw through pilot.
3.

### Index camshaft bearing in bore (with oil hole aligned as
`chevrolet_camaro_en_8d707c67` | camaro | pdf_manual | tier:3 | lang:en | layer:engine | p:140

outlined below), then install remover and installer tool
on puller screw with shoulder toward bearing.
a.
In Line Engines-All cam bearing oil holes must be
aligned with oil hole in cam bore.
b.
Small V8 Engines-Number one cam bearing oil
hole must be positioned so that oil holes are equidis­
tant from 6 o’clock position. Number two through
number four bearing oil holes must be positioned at
5 o" clock position (toward left side of engine and at
a position even with bottom of cylinder bore). Num­
ber five bearing oil hole must be in 12 o" clock posi­
tion.
c.

### Mark IV V8 Engines-Number one through number
`chevrolet_camaro_en_811efb76` | camaro | pdf_manual | tier:3 | lang:en | layer:general | p:140

four cam bearing oil hole must be aligned with oil
holes in cam bearing bore. The number five bearing
bore is annulus and cam bearing must be positioned
at or near the 6 o" clock position.

### CYLINDER BLOCK
`chevrolet_camaro_en_aaa1b025` | camaro | pdf_manual | tier:3 | lang:en | layer:engine | p:141

3.
Clean and inspect water passages in the cylinder block.
4.
Inspect the cylinder block for cracks in the cylinder
walls, water jacket valve lifter bores and main bearing
webs.
5.
Measure the cylinder walls for taper, out-of-round or
excessive ridge at top of ring travel. This should be done
with a dial indicator. Set the gauge so that the thrust pin
must be forced in about 1/4" to enter gauge in cylinder
bore. Center gauge in cylinder and turn dial to "0".

### Carefully work gauge up and down cylinder to deter­
`chevrolet_camaro_en_97ff1cc2` | camaro | pdf_manual | tier:3 | lang:en | layer:engine | p:141

mine taper and turn it to different points around cylin­
der wall to determine the out-of-round condition. If
cylinders were found to exceed specifications, honing or
boring will be necessary (fig. 70).

### Oil Filter Bypass Valve
`chevrolet_camaro_en_2787d126` | camaro | pdf_manual | tier:3 | lang:en | layer:engine | p:141

Inspection and Replacement
IN-LINE ENGINES
With the oil filter removed, check the spring and fibre
valve for operation. Inspect for a cracked or broken valve. If
replacement is necessary, remove valve by prying it out with
a screw driver. Install and seat a new valve by tapping it in
place, using a 9/16 thin-wall deep socket (fig. 71).

### V8 ENGINES
`chevrolet_camaro_en_6ab417f3` | camaro | pdf_manual | tier:3 | lang:en | layer:engine | p:141

With the oil filter removed, check the spring and fibre
valve for operation. Inspect for a cracked or broken valve. If
replacement is necessary, the oil filter adapter and bypass
valve assembly must be replaced as an assembly. Clean valve
chamber in cylinder block thoroughly. Torque retaining
screws to specifications (fig. 72).

### Cleaning and Inspection
`chevrolet_camaro_en_82b998ba` | camaro | pdf_manual | tier:3 | lang:en | layer:engine | p:141

1.
Wash cylinder block thoroughly in cleaning solvent and
clean all gasket surfaces.
2.
Remove oil gallery plugs and clean all oil passages.
NOTE: These plugs may be removed with a sharp
punch or they may be drilled and pried out.

### Fig. 70-M easuring Cylinder Bore
`chevrolet_camaro_en_4e752b61` | camaro | pdf_manual | tier:3 | lang:en | layer:engine | p:141

CHEVROLET OVERHAUL MANUAL
ENGINE 6-34
Fig. 71-O il Filter By-Pass Valve (In-Line)
Distributor Lower Bearing and Thrust Washer
Replacement (In Line)
The distributor lower bearing is a bronze bushing pressed
into the lower side of the engine block. Its upper inside
diameter pilots the distributor shaft and the outside diameter
extending below the block pilots the oil pump.

### Some engines have a thrust washer at the upper end of the
`chevrolet_camaro_en_742b9806` | camaro | pdf_manual | tier:3 | lang:en | layer:engine | p:142

bushing bore. The thrust washer, where used, may be re­
placed at the same time the bushing is replaced.
The lower bushing will ordinarily require only a clearance
or wear check during engine overhaul. When distributor
shaft-to-bushing clearance exceeds .0035" the bushing
should be replaced as follows:
1.

### With oil pump and distributor removed install Tool
`chevrolet_camaro_en_0f60a727` | camaro | pdf_manual | tier:3 | lang:en | layer:general | p:142

J-9534 into bushing and using a slide hammer, remove
the bushing (fig. 73).
2.
Using a drift up through bushing bore, drive thrust
washer (if installed) out of bore and remove from block.
3.
Clean bushing bore in block and check for burrs or
damage.
4.

### If thrust washer was removed, start new washer in
`chevrolet_camaro_en_0e153171` | camaro | pdf_manual | tier:3 | lang:en | layer:general | p:142

position in bore and drive into place using J-9535.
Fig. 72-O il Filter By-Pass Valve (V8)
Fig. 73-Replacing Distributor Bearing and Thrust Washer
5.
Using Tool J-9535 with driver-bolt in driver handle
install driver into new bushing from large inside diame­
ter.
6.

### Position bushing and driver to block and drive the
`chevrolet_camaro_en_23c5a919` | camaro | pdf_manual | tier:3 | lang:en | layer:general | p:142

bushing in position, which is determined by tool bot­
toming against the block.
7.
Remove tool from bushing. It is possible that the bush­
ing with minimum I.D. will collapse enough during
installation to slightly seize the installer arbor. If this
happens, remove installer tool using slide hammer in
driver bolt hole or driver handle.

### NOTE: This will not damage the bushing and tool is
`chevrolet_camaro_en_39e077df` | camaro | pdf_manual | tier:3 | lang:en | layer:engine | p:142

designed for this purpose, should it occur.
Repairs
CYLINDER CONDITIONING
The performance of the following operation is contingent
upon engine condition at time of repair.
If the cylinder block inspection indicated that the block
was suitable for continued use except for out-of-round or
tapered cylinders, they can be conditioned by honing or bor­
ing.

### If the cylinders were found to have less than .005" taper
`chevrolet_camaro_en_ec13a8d1` | camaro | pdf_manual | tier:3 | lang:en | layer:engine | p:142

or wear they can be conditioned with a hone and fitted with
the high limit standard size piston. A cylinder bore of less
then .005" wear or taper may not entirely clean up when
fitted to a high limit piston. If it is desired to entirely clean
up the bore in these cases, it will be necessary to rebore for

### CHEVROLET OVERHAUL MANUAL
`chevrolet_camaro_en_ff0d44c5` | camaro | pdf_manual | tier:3 | lang:en | layer:engine | p:142

ENGINE 6-35
an oversize piston. If more than .005" taper or wear, they
should be bored and honed to the smallest oversize that will
permit complete resurfacing of all cylinders.
When pistons are being fitted and honing is not necessary,
cylinder bores may be cleaned with a hot water and detergent
wash. After cleaning, the cylinder bores should be swabbed
several times with light engine oil and a clean cloth and then
wiped with a clean dry cloth.

### CYLINDER BORING
`chevrolet_camaro_en_8fe8e849` | camaro | pdf_manual | tier:3 | lang:en | layer:engine | p:143

1.
Before using any type boring bar, the top of the cylinder
block should be filed off to remove any dirt or burrs.
This is very important. Otherwise, the boring bar may
be tilted which would result in the rebored cylinder wall
not being at right angles to the crankshaft.
3.

### When finish honing a cylinder bore to fit a piston, the
`chevrolet_camaro_en_b823b6da` | camaro | pdf_manual | tier:3 | lang:en | layer:general | p:143

hone should be moved up and down at a sufficient speed
to obtain very fine uniform surface finish marks in a
cross-hatch pattern of approximately 45° to 65° in­
cluded angle. The finish marks should be clean but not
sharp, free from imbedded particles and torn or folded
metal (fig. 74).
4.

### Permanently mark the piston for the cylinder to which
`chevrolet_camaro_en_7f7397a6` | camaro | pdf_manual | tier:3 | lang:en | layer:engine | p:143

it has been fitted and proceed to hone cylinders and fit
the remaining pistons.
CAUTION: Handle the pistons with care and do not
attempt to force them through the cylinder until the
cylinder has been honed to correct size as this type
piston can be distorted through careless handling.
2.

### The piston to be fitted should be measured with a mi­
`chevrolet_camaro_en_2bddd98a` | camaro | pdf_manual | tier:3 | lang:en | layer:engine | p:143

crometer, measuring at the center of the piston skirt and
at right angles to the piston pin. The cylinder should be
bored to the same diameter as the piston and honed to
give the specified clearance.
NOTE: Hone cylinders as outlined under "Cylinder

### Honing and Piston Fitting".
`chevrolet_camaro_en_4ecd7ed3` | camaro | pdf_manual | tier:3 | lang:en | layer:engine | p:143

3.
The instructions furnished by the manufacturer of the
equipment being used should be carefully followed.
5.
Throughly clean the bores with hot water and deter­
gent. Scrub well with a stiff bristle brush and rinse
thoroughly with hot water. It is extremely essential that
a good cleaning operation be performed. If any of the
abrasive material is allowed to remain in the cylinder
bores, it will rapidly wear the new rings and cylinder
bores in addition to the bearings lubricated by the con­
taminated oil, the bores should be swabbed several
times with light engine oil and a clean cloth and then
wiped with a clean dry cloth. Cylinder should not be
cleaned with kerosene or gasoline. Clean the remainder
of the cylinder block to remove the excess material
spread during the honing operation.

### CYLINDER HONING
`chevrolet_camaro_en_b21b5c0b` | camaro | pdf_manual | tier:3 | lang:en | layer:engine | p:143

1.
When cylinders are to be honed follow the hone manu­
facturer’s recommendations for the use of the hone and
cleaning and lubrication during honing.
2.
Occasionally during the honing operation, the cylinder
bore should be thoroughly cleaned and the piston se­
lected for the individual cylinder checked for correct fit.

### Fig. 74-C ylinder Finish Marks
`chevrolet_camaro_en_e2f3e158` | camaro | pdf_manual | tier:3 | lang:en | layer:engine | p:143

PISTON SELECTION
1.
Check USED piston to cylinder bore clearance as fol­
lows:
a.
Measure the "Cylinder Bore Diameter" with a tele­
scope guage (2-1/ 2" from top of cylinder bore).
b.

ter line of piston pin).
c.

Chart (fig. 75) and determine if piston to bore clear­
ance is in the acceptable range.

INTRODUCTION

### HO LLEY CARBU RETO RS IDENTIFICATION, FIG. S2)
`chevrolet_camaro_en_0b2fbdf8` | camaro | pdf_manual | tier:3 | lang:en | layer:engine | p:149

Various carburetors, designed to meet the particular re­
quirements of engines, transmission and vehicles, are used on
passenger vehicles and although carburetors may look alike
they are not always interchangeable. Refer to carburetor part
number and/or specifications.

### This section, divided into sub-sections by carburetor
`chevrolet_camaro_en_97f116ce` | camaro | pdf_manual | tier:3 | lang:en | layer:general | p:149

model, covers the repair procedures for the various carburet­
ors, assembly and disassembly procedures and internal car­
buretor adjustment. Although illustrations showing bench
operations are used, most single operations, when not part of

### ROCHESTER M AND
`chevrolet_camaro_en_ea522b6f` | camaro | pdf_manual | tier:3 | lang:en | layer:engine | p:149

INDEX
a general overhaul, should be performed (if practical) with
the carburetor on the engine. Typical illustrations and proce­
dures are used except where specific illustrations or proce­
dures are necessary to clarify the operation.

### Air Horn Assembly and Installation................. 6M-9
`chevrolet_camaro_en_b7ebbaa3` | camaro | pdf_manual | tier:3 | lang:en | layer:engine | p:149

GENERAL DESCRIPTION
The model MV (Fig. M2) carburetor used on the Chev­
rolet, 6 cylinder engine is a single bore, down draft unit using
a triple venturi in conjunction with a plain tube nozzle. The
main venturi is 1 5/16" in diameter and the throttle bore is
1 11/16".

### Fuel flow through the main metering system is controlled
`chevrolet_camaro_en_e75273f2` | camaro | pdf_manual | tier:3 | lang:en | layer:engine | p:149

by a main well air bleed and a variable orifice jet. A power
enrichment system is used to provide good performance dur­
ing moderate to heavy acceleration and at higher engine
speeds.
The idle system incorporates a ho. idle compensator to
maintain smooth engine idle during periods of extreme hot
engine operation.

### 'M’ TYPE
`chevrolet_camaro_en_298a964c` | camaro | pdf_manual | tier:3 | lang:en | layer:general | p:150

'2G’ TYPE

Fig. M 1-Rochester Carburetors Identification
CARBURETOR 6M-3
The model MV carburetor has an automatic choke system.
The vacuum diaphragm unit is an integral part of the air
horn. The choke coil is mounted on the manifold and is
connected to the choke valve shaft by a rod.

### An internal fuel inlet filter is mounted in the fuel bowl
`chevrolet_camaro_en_b65312c8` | camaro | pdf_manual | tier:3 | lang:en | layer:engine | p:151

behind the fuel inlet nut to give maximum filtration of incom­
ing fuel.
Other features of the model MV include an aluminum
throttle body and a thick throttle body to bowl insulator
gasket. The carburetor has internally balanced venting
through a vent hole in the air horn which leads from the float
bowl into the bore beneath the air cleaner. The float bowl is
externally vented through a pressure relief valve system
which allows vapors to be vented during hot engine operat­
ion.

### The carburetor part number is stamped on a vertical sec­
`chevrolet_camaro_en_d81cdc0b` | camaro | pdf_manual | tier:3 | lang:en | layer:general | p:151

tion of the float bowl, next to the fuel inlet nut. When replac­
ing the float bowl assembly, follow the manufacturer’s
instructions contained in the service package so that the part
number can be transferred to the new float bowl.

### The idle stop solenoid has been replaced by a combination
`chevrolet_camaro_en_b1f19ee0` | camaro | pdf_manual | tier:3 | lang:en | layer:engine | p:151

emission control valve (C.E.C. valve). The valve, when ener­
gized through the transmission, acts as a throttle stop by
increasing idle speed during high gear operation of the engine
which helps in controlling overrun hydrocarbons during de­
celeration. The C.E.C. valve also provides full spark vacuum
advance during high gear operation and is de-energized in the
lower gears and at idle, for retarded spark timing during this
period. Normal idle speed setting will be made with the idle
stop screw.
The idle mixture screw will have a limiter cap installed and
no adjustment will be provided on the vehicle. The mixture
screw will be pre-set at the factory and capped, and no fur­
ther adjustment should be required except during the clean­
ing &nd overhaul.

### An overhaul idle mixture adjustment procedure will be
`chevrolet_camaro_en_402fc9af` | camaro | pdf_manual | tier:3 | lang:en | layer:general | p:151

provided, should the idle mixture needle need replacement or
the mixture channels cleaned during the overhaul process. A
new idle mixture needle limiter cap will be provided in the
overhaul kit.

`chevrolet_camaro_en_0fbf785e` | camaro | pdf_manual | tier:3 | lang:en | layer:brakes | p:151

NOTE: Do not remove C.E.C. valve bracket from the
float bowl assembly unless replacement of the
bracket is necessary. Complete replacement in­
structions are included in the replacement bracket
kit.

### CAUTION: Do not immerse the C.E.C. valve assem­
`chevrolet_camaro_en_ae4f4bf0` | camaro | pdf_manual | tier:3 | lang:en | layer:general | p:151

bly in any type of carburetor cleaner.

2.

### Remove six air horn to float bowl attaching screws.
`chevrolet_camaro_en_d678c2de` | camaro | pdf_manual | tier:3 | lang:en | layer:general | p:154

3.
Remove air horn by lifting straight up. Invert air horn
and place on clean bench. Air horn to bowl gasket can
remain on bowl for removal later.
Air Horn Disassembly
1.
Remove two vacuum break diaphragm cover screws.

### Then carefully remove diaphragm cover.
`chevrolet_camaro_en_c5174dcd` | camaro | pdf_manual | tier:3 | lang:en | layer:general | p:154

2.
To remove vacuum break diaphragm and plunger rod,
hold choke valve wide open. Then push upward on
eyelet on choke valve at a 45 degree angle until the
looped end of rod slides off wire lever attached to the
choke valve. Then remove diaphragm and plunger rod
assembly through the hole in air horn. (Figure M4).
3.

### If desired, the choke valve, vacuum break lever, and
`chevrolet_camaro_en_0453deba` | camaro | pdf_manual | tier:3 | lang:en | layer:general | p:154

choke shaft can be removed from air horn by first
removing the thermostatic coil lever from the end of
choke shaft, by removing the attaching screw. After
removing the thermostatic coil lever, remove the two
choke valve attaching screws; then remove the choke
valve and choke shaft from air horn.

### NOTE: The choke valve screws are held in place by
`chevrolet_camaro_en_9160e408` | camaro | pdf_manual | tier:3 | lang:en | layer:general | p:154

lock-tite so it will be necessary to re-stake after as­
sembly.
Float Bowl Disassembly
1.
Remove air horn to float bowl gasket. Gasket is slit next
to metering rod hanger so that it can be easily removed.
2.

### Remove float assembly from float bowl by lifting up­
`chevrolet_camaro_en_bf3f4b35` | camaro | pdf_manual | tier:3 | lang:en | layer:interior | p:154

ward on float hinge pin. Remove hinge pin from float
arm.
3.
Remove float needle, float needle seat and gasket. Use
caution in removing needle seat to prevent damage.
4.
Remove fuel inlet nut, gasket, paper filter element and
pressure relief spring.
5.

### Using long nosed pliers, remove "T" pump discharge
`chevrolet_camaro_en_ce99944b` | camaro | pdf_manual | tier:3 | lang:en | layer:general | p:154

spring retainer. Pump discharge spring and ball may be
removed by inverting bowl.
6.
The idle tube can be removed at same time by inverting
bowl.
7.
To remove accelerating pump plunger and metering
rod-pow er piston drive assemblies, perform following
operation:
a.

### Remove actuating lever on throttle shaft by remov­
`chevrolet_camaro_en_0529c516` | camaro | pdf_manual | tier:3 | lang:en | layer:general | p:154

ing attaching screw at end of shaft.
b.
Remove upper end of drive link from power piston
rod.
c.
Rotate drive link from keyhole in actuating lever.
d.
Remove actuating lever from pump link by rotating
off tang on rod.
e.

### Remove upper end of pump link by rotating from
`chevrolet_camaro_en_c653aea9` | camaro | pdf_manual | tier:3 | lang:en | layer:general | p:154

keyhole in pump slide.
8.
The power piston—metering rod assembly and drive rod
can now be lifted from float bowl.
9.
Remove power piston spring from power piston cavity.
10.
Remove pump plunger assembly from float bowl.
11.

### Remove pump return spring from pump well.
`chevrolet_camaro_en_3ad27e87` | camaro | pdf_manual | tier:3 | lang:en | layer:general | p:154

12.
Remove main metering jet from bottom of fuel bowl.
13.
Remove two screws from idle compensator cover. Then
remove cover, hot idle compensator and gasket from
recess in bowl beneath compensator.
14.

### Idle adjustment screw and fast idle cam can be removed
`chevrolet_camaro_en_d5f840e1` | camaro | pdf_manual | tier:3 | lang:en | layer:body | p:154

at this time if desired. No further disassembly of the
float bowl is required.
Throttle Body Removal and Disassembly
1.
Invert carburetor bowl on bench and remove two throt­
tle body to bowl attaching screws. Throttle body and
insulator gasket may now be removed from float bowl.

### NOTE: Do not tamper with the idle mixture needle
`chevrolet_camaro_en_6500421e` | camaro | pdf_manual | tier:3 | lang:en | layer:body | p:154

with a limiter cap unless performing an overhaul or
CHEVROLET OVERHAUL MANUAL
CARBURETOR 6M-7
due to needle damage. This has been set to test re­
quirements by the manufacturer.
2.
N o further disassembly of the throttle body is nec­
essary unless the idle m ixture needle is dam aged
or the idle channels need cleaning. If necessary to
rem ove the idle m ixture needle, destroy plastic
lim iter cap as a new one is provided in the over­
haul kit.

### IMPORTANT: If CO Reading equipment is not avail­
`chevrolet_camaro_en_262e2f8d` | camaro | pdf_manual | tier:3 | lang:en | layer:general | p:155

able, before removing idle mixture needle, be certain
to count number of turns to bottom the old idle mix­
ture needle. This is required so that when it is neces­
sary to install a new needle, you may bottom the
new needle and then back off the same number of
turns it took to bottom the old needle.
3.

### Rem ove the idle m ixture needle and spring, if
`chevrolet_camaro_en_098016f2` | camaro | pdf_manual | tier:3 | lang:en | layer:body | p:155

required.
NOTE: Due to the close tolerance fit of throttle
valve in the bore of the throttle body, do not remove
the valve or shaft.
Cleaning and inspection
The carburetor should be cleaned in a cold immersion
type cleaner.
1.

### Thoroughly clean carburetor castings and metal parts
`chevrolet_camaro_en_47e3ce8a` | camaro | pdf_manual | tier:3 | lang:en | layer:general | p:155

in an approved carburetor cleaner.
CAUTION:
Any rubber parts, plastic parts, dia­
phragms, pump plunger, electric parts and solenoids
should not be immersed in carburetor cleaner. How­
ever, the air horn which was the pressure relief
valve will withstand normal cleaning in carburetor
cleaner. Make sure the cleaning solution is
thoroughly removed from pressure relief valve area.
2.

### Blow out all passages in castings with compressed air.
`chevrolet_camaro_en_d5f6744b` | camaro | pdf_manual | tier:3 | lang:en | layer:interior | p:155

Do not pass drills through jets or passages.
3.
Inspect idle mixture needle for damage.
4.
Examine float needle and seat assembly for wear. Install
a new factory matched set if worn.
5.
Inspect upper and lower casting sealing surfaces for
damage.
6.

### Inspect holes in levers for excessive wear or out of
`chevrolet_camaro_en_1b1043b0` | camaro | pdf_manual | tier:3 | lang:en | layer:general | p:155

round condition. If levers or rods are worn they should
be replaced.
7.
Examine fast idle cam for excessive wear or damage.
8.
Check throttle and choke levers and valves for binds
and other damage.
9.

### Replace filter element.
`chevrolet_camaro_en_ef1314c1` | camaro | pdf_manual | tier:3 | lang:en | layer:body | p:155

10.
Check all springs for distortion or loss in tension, re­
place as necessary.
CARBURETOR ASSEMBLY
Throttle Body Assembly
New Part Replacement
If a new throttle body is being replaced, install and bottom
the new idle mixture needle and back off four turns. Do not
install plastic limiter cap at this time until proper screw
settings have been made.

### After completing assembly of the carburetor, and when
`chevrolet_camaro_en_46d5f4dc` | camaro | pdf_manual | tier:3 | lang:en | layer:general | p:155

installed in the vehicle, adjust the mixture screw to achieve
the required percent of "CO" in the exhaust gas (see Service
Manual under, "Additional External Settings and Adjust­
ments") -which is the recommended method; however, if
equipment for a "CO" reading is not available, you may set
the idle speed and idle mixture settings as outlined also under
"Additional External Settings and Adjustments".
1.

### If removed, install idle mixture needle and spring until
`chevrolet_camaro_en_c8fb9368` | camaro | pdf_manual | tier:3 | lang:en | layer:engine | p:155

lightly seated. Back out four turns as a preliminary idle
adjustment.
NOTE: The plastic limiter cap should not be installed
on the idle mixture needle until the idle mixture has
been adjusted, as specified, on the engine.

### NOTE: A new red plastic idle mixture needle limiter
`chevrolet_camaro_en_e08952b8` | camaro | pdf_manual | tier:3 | lang:en | layer:engine | p:155

cap is provided in the carburetor repair kit and also
in the idle mixture needle and limiter cap kit. This
cap must be installed after the idle mixture needle
has been set on engine by the CO reading (see

### Specifications), or another method may be used, by
`chevrolet_camaro_en_39ecffb2` | camaro | pdf_manual | tier:3 | lang:en | layer:general | p:155

backing off the new mixture needle the same num­
ber of turns, after bottoming, as was required to
bottom the original needle which was pre-set and
sealed by the manufacturer before it left the factory.
(See"Note" in disassembly procedures).
2.

insulator gasket.

Install throttle body on bowl gasket so that all holes in
throttle body are aligned with holes in gasket.

Install two throttle body to bowl attaching screws.
Tighten evenly and securely (12 to 15 foot lbs. of

lock washers as they have an interference fit designed
into the thread for holding proper torque.

### GENERAL DESCRIPTION
`chevrolet_camaro_en_8577b615` | camaro | pdf_manual | tier:3 | lang:en | layer:general | p:157

The Rochester Models 2G and 2GV carburetors (fig. G1
and G2) are used in conjunction with a temperature sensing
choke coil (mounted on the intake manifold over the exhaust
crossover passage).
These are two barrel carburetors with two venturi and a
separate fuel feed for each. All fuel metering is centerally
located so that each system will give instantaneous response
for maximum efficiency and performance.

### CHEVROLET OVERHAUL MANUAL
`chevrolet_camaro_en_ba2c63bd` | camaro | pdf_manual | tier:3 | lang:en | layer:engine | p:157

6M-10 CARBURETOR
The removable venturi cluster contains the main nozzles,
idle tubes, mixture passages, air bleeds and pump jets. The
main nozzles and idle tubes are suspended in the main wells
of the float bowl which helps insulate them from engine heat
and to minimize percolation spill over during hot engine
operation (fig. G4 and G5).

### On air conditioned passenger cars and trucks with auto­
`chevrolet_camaro_en_99c1acdf` | camaro | pdf_manual | tier:3 | lang:en | layer:drivetrain | p:158

matic transmission the carburetor contains a hot idle com­
pensator (fig. G3). The hot idle compensator consisting of a
bi-metal strip, a valve and a mounting bracket located in a
cavity at the rear of the carburetor bowl is a thermostatically
controlled air bleed, which supplies additional air to the idle
mixture during prolonged hot idle periods.

The Rochester models 2G and 2GV carburetors are used
in two different sizes for Chevrolet engines. The SAE 1 1/4"
model is used on the 307" (light duty) V-8 engine. The SAE
1 1/2" model is used on the 307" Heavy Duty and the larger
350" and 400" V-8 engines for increased air capacity.

### The Model 2G and 2GV carburetors have the following
`chevrolet_camaro_en_f2cfc364` | camaro | pdf_manual | tier:3 | lang:en | layer:engine | p:159

changes for 1971:
1.
Calibration for 1971 engines.
2.
New choke shaft lever with increased off-set for remove
choke link on 2GV V-8 models.
3.
Dam added to air horn on 1 1/4" truck models to
reduce fuel slosh and improve vapor handling.
4.

### Two stage power valve to provide additional fuel at
`chevrolet_camaro_en_9a64dbdf` | camaro | pdf_manual | tier:3 | lang:en | layer:general | p:159

wide-open throttle on 1 1/ 2 " truck models.
5.
Timed ported vacuum on all 2GV models to operate
purge valve on the vapor canister.
6.
Seven short air horn screws changed to self-locking
thread type for improved torque retention.
7.

### External carburetor venting has been eliminated from
`chevrolet_camaro_en_dd25aab1` | camaro | pdf_manual | tier:3 | lang:en | layer:body | p:159

all passenger and 1 1/4" truck applications to meet
1971 State and Federal requirements for Evaporative
Emissions. Similar to 1970 California 2GV models, va­
por vent holes, vented throttle body gaskets (where
used), and idle vent valves have been eliminated (except
on 20 and 30 Series). The float bowl is internally vented
by a large hole or tube which leads from inside air horn
bore to the top of the fuel in the float bowl. The carbu­
retor is internally balanced through the internal vent so
that the same pressure causing air to flow will be acting
upon the top of the fuel in the float bowl causing the
correct fuel to flow.

### 8. A supplem entary fuel feed passage, called A djust­
`chevrolet_camaro_en_5db29d8e` | camaro | pdf_manual | tier:3 | lang:en | layer:general | p:159

able Part Throttle (A.P.T.) is located in the bottom
of the float bowl, next to the m ain m etering jets,
on all 2G and 2GV models. Fuel passes down
through this passage, past a calibration screw, on
into the pow er valve cavity and then passes on
into the m ain fuel wells to supplem ent the fuel
passing through the calibrated m ain m etering jets.

### T he calibration screw, located in the supplem en­
`chevrolet_camaro_en_b76af953` | camaro | pdf_manual | tier:3 | lang:en | layer:general | p:159

tary fuel feed passage, is factory adjusted and
should not be readjusted in the field.
9.
A new garter spring accelerator pum p is used on
1 W  2GV m odel carburetors. The new pum p uses
a pum p cup garter spring to m aintain constant
pum p cup to pum p wall contact. The pum p cup is
the self-venting “floating” type. A new  d u ratio n
spring and pum p return spring are used w ith the
new pum p.
10.

### On the 1 1/4" and 1 1/2" 2GV model carburetors
`chevrolet_camaro_en_7a009383` | camaro | pdf_manual | tier:3 | lang:en | layer:engine | p:159

(except 1 1/ 2" truck), the throttle closing solenoid has
been replaced by a Combination Emission Control
Valve (C.E.C. Valve). The C.E.C. valve with bracket is
mounted on the carburetor float bowl. The valve, when
energized through the transmission, acts as a throttle
stop by increasing idle speed of the engine during high
gear operation to help in controlling overrun hydrocar­
bons during deceleration. Further, the C.E.C. valve
controls distributor vacuum spark advance by provid­
ing full spark vacuum advance during transmission
high gear operation, and retarded spark timing during
operation in the transmission lower gears and at idle.

### Normal idle speed setting is made with the idle stop
`chevrolet_camaro_en_2f1a7921` | camaro | pdf_manual | tier:3 | lang:en | layer:engine | p:159

screw. Idle speed settings should be made using emis­
sion control information on the label located in the
engine compartment.
11.
Idle mixture needle limiters are installed on all 2G and
2GV model carburetors except 1 1/2" truck. The cor­
rect engine idle mixture will be set to a calibration at the
factory for each engine application. Then, a plastic cap
is installed over the head of the mixture needle. No
adjustment will be provided on the vehicle. If the limiter
cap, idle needle and spring are removed for cleaning and
inspection, follow the car manufacturer’s specifications
for the idle mixture adjustment. Service replacement
idle mixture needle limiter caps will be colored red to
indicate a field replacement has been made.
12.

### All 2GV models have no provision for transfer of ex­
`chevrolet_camaro_en_0e55c915` | camaro | pdf_manual | tier:3 | lang:en | layer:body | p:159

haust manifold heat to the carburetor through a heat
passage in the throttle body.
O n 2G V  m odels using the C.E.C. valve, a 3 /1 6 "
tube has been added to the throttle body betw een
the idle needles. This supplies vacuum  to the

### C.E.C. valve for full d istributor vacuum advance
`chevrolet_camaro_en_f087d020` | camaro | pdf_manual | tier:3 | lang:en | layer:body | p:159

during high gear operation. The throttle body
casting has been revised to provide extended p as­
sages for tracking crankcase vapors to the intake
m anifold from  the Positive C rankcase V entilator
Valve (P.C.V .). Also, a 1/4" pipe tap is included
at the rear o f the th ro ttle body on all passenger
car 2GV m odels as an accessory vacuum  source.
13.

### The choke system is changed on 2GV V8 models in
`chevrolet_camaro_en_6cfb05b3` | camaro | pdf_manual | tier:3 | lang:en | layer:engine | p:159

that a delayed vacuum break system is used. The system
operates as follows: When the engine is started, vacuum
is applied to the choke vacuum diaphragm which opens
the choke valve, against the choke coil tension, to a
point where the engine will run without loading or
stalling lean. To delay the choke valve from opening too
fast, an internal check valve is used in the choke
vacuum diaphragm unit. After the engine starts,
vacuum is applied through the check valve to the
vacuum break diaphragm causing the vacuum break
diaphragm plunger to move slowly inward. This gives
sufficient time to overcome engine friction and allow
the engine manifold to be wetted to prevent a lean stall.

W hen the vacuum  break diaphragm  is fully seated,
the choke valve will rem ain in the vacuum  break
p osition until the engine begins to w arm  up and
the exhaust heat w arm s the R em ote C hoke T her­
m o static Coil. T he exh au st h eat th en  begins to
relax the tension of the choke coil. This allows the
choke valve to open gradually th ro u g h  air flow
against the off-set choke valve, until the engine is
warm  and the choke valve is fully open.

### A choke closing assist spring has been ad d ed to
`chevrolet_camaro_en_b461ec4c` | camaro | pdf_manual | tier:3 | lang:en | layer:engine | p:162

the vacuum  break diaphragm  plunger stem . The
spring assists in closing the choke valve, along
w ith tension from  the rem ote choke therm ostatic
coil, for im proved cold starting. The choke closing
assist spring only exerts pressure on the vacuum
break link to assist in closing the choke valve
during engine starting.

### W hen the engine starts and the ch o k e vacuum
`chevrolet_camaro_en_2a14b7ee` | camaro | pdf_manual | tier:3 | lang:en | layer:body | p:162

break diaphragm  seats, the closing spring retainer
hits a stop on the plunger stem  and no longer
exerts pressure on the vacuum  break link.

### CAUTION: Do not immerse the C.E.C. valve assem­

bly in any type of carburetor cleaner.
Disassemble Air Horn (Fig. G7)
1.
Remove choke coil lever retaining screw from the end
of choke shaft and disengage choke lever from vacuum
break diaphragm link. Then remove the vacuum break
4.
5.
6.

### Disconnect vacuum break diaphragm hose from tube
`chevrolet_camaro_en_b245c1da` | camaro | pdf_manual | tier:3 | lang:en | layer:body | p:162

on throttle body, then remove vacuum break dia­
phragm from air horn by removing two retaining

Place carburetor on a clean bench, being careful not to
damage throttle valves. Then remove the fuel inlet filter
nut, filter, spring and two gaskets.

### Remove pump rod retaining clip from the throttle lever
`chevrolet_camaro_en_8adf01e7` | camaro | pdf_manual | tier:3 | lang:en | layer:general | p:162

end of rod, and remove rod from throttle lever. Rotate
upper pump lever counterclockwise, then remove the
pump rod from the pump lever by aligning squirt on rod

Using a wide bladed screwdriver, remove the fast idle
cam attaching screw rotate cam and remove from rod.

### Hold choke valve wide open, then rotate the upper end
`chevrolet_camaro_en_4d3f5f26` | camaro | pdf_manual | tier:3 | lang:en | layer:general | p:162

kets.

the center screw is not threaded the full length of

necessary to replace the mixture needles or clean the

miter caps are provided in the repair kits. They should
not be installed until after the idle mixture has been

The carburetor should be cleaned in a cold immersion
type cleaner.

in an approved carburetor cleaner.

Any rubber parts, plastic parts, dia­
phragms, pump plunger, electric parts and solenoids
should not be immersed in carburetor cleaner. How­
ever, the air horn which has the pressure relief valve
will withstand normal darning in carburetor
cleaner. Make sure the cleaning solution is
thoroughly removed from pressure relief valve area.

Assemble Bowl and Throttle Body
1.
If it was necessary to remove the idle mixture adjusting
needles and springs, install them into the throttle body
until finger tight. Back out screw four turns as a
preliminary idle mixture adjustment.

### D o not install the idle m ixture lim iter caps u ntil

the idle m ixture has been reset w ith the c a rb u r­
eto r installed  on the engine per in stru ctio n s in ­
cluded in the service m anual.

against the seat or damage will result.

If a new throttle body is being replaced, install and bottom

install plastic limiter cap at this time until proper screw
settings have been made.

aligning holes in gasket with holes in the float bowl, and
attached throttle body to bowl with the attaching

NOTE: A new red plastic idle mixture needle limiter

in the idle mixture needle and limiter cap kit. This
cap must be installed after the idle mixture needle
has been set on engine by the CO reading (see

right.

facing upward. Install choke valve screws. Before tight­
ening the choke valve screws, make sure that there is
.020" clearance between the choke kick lever on the air
horn casting. Then tighten the choke valve screw se­
curely and stake in place to eliminate any possibility of
their coming loose.

### Install accelerator pump plunger and rod to the inner

driver. Place the float needle into needle seat.

### Install air horn to float bowl gasket. Align position

9.
Install fuel filter spring, fuel filter, filter gasket, fuel
inlet nut gasket and fuel inlet nut. Torque inlet nut
sufficiently to seat gasket. Install vacuum break dia­
phragm assembly on to air horn with the part number
on bracket facing outward. Install two attaching screws
and tighten securely. Insert off-set and vacuum break
diaphragm rod into plunger on vacuum break dia­
phragm. Then install other end of rod to hole in choke
coil lever. Install choke coil lever on to end of choke
shaft aligining flats on lever with flats on shaft. Install
retaining screw into the end of choke shaft and tighen
securely. Part number on choke coil lever face outward
when installed correctly.

tube on throttle body, then remove vacuum diaphragm

cam attaching screw-rotate cam and remove cam from

dle seat and gasket.

### Disassembly of Float Bowl and Throttle
`chevrolet_camaro_en_1aa28a16` | camaro | pdf_manual | tier:3 | lang:en | layer:body | p:171

Body (Figure V3)
1.
Remove the pump plunger return spring from pump
well.
2.
Remove main metering jets and power valve and gas­
ket.
3.
Remove three screws on top of cluster after which clus­
ter and gasket may be removed.

### NOTE: The cluster center screw has two fiber wash­
`chevrolet_camaro_en_0a7cb4d1` | camaro | pdf_manual | tier:3 | lang:en | layer:body | p:171

ers and a baffle located just above the main well air
bleeds. The two outer screws have lock washers.
Also, the center screw is not threaded the full length
of the body -- smaller diameter is required for pump
jet discharge. The high speed bleed baffle must be
installed between the two fiber gaskets underneath
the head of center cluster screw.
4.

### Using a pair of long nose pliers, remove the pump dis­
`chevrolet_camaro_en_77179a3e` | camaro | pdf_manual | tier:3 | lang:en | layer:general | p:171

charge spring retainer (Figure V4). Then the pump dis­
charge spring and check ball may also be removed.
NOTE: Do not tamper with the idle mixture needle
with a limiter cap unless performing an overhaul or
due to needle damage. This has been set to test re­
quirements by the manufacturer.
7.

### Further disassembly of the throttle body is not recom­
`chevrolet_camaro_en_03f85bc2` | camaro | pdf_manual | tier:3 | lang:en | layer:general | p:171

mended. If the idle mixture needles are damaged, or
need replacement or the idle mixture channels have to
be cleaned, the plastic limiter cap should be broken
away from mixture screws as new ones are provided in

### IMPORTANT: If CO Reading equipment is not avail­
`chevrolet_camaro_en_4577a760` | camaro | pdf_manual | tier:3 | lang:en | layer:general | p:171

able, before removing idle mixture needle, be certain
to count number of turns to bottom this old idle mix­
ture needle. This is required so that when it is neces­
sary to install a new needle, you may bottom the
new needle and then back off the same number of
turns it took to bottom the old needle.

### 8. Remove idle mixture needle and spring, if required.
`chevrolet_camaro_en_308f4b70` | camaro | pdf_manual | tier:3 | lang:en | layer:general | p:171

Cleaning and Inspection
CAUTION: Do not immerse the C.E.C. valve in any
type of carburetor cleaner or solvent.
The carburetor should be cleaned in a cold immersion type
cleaner.
1.
Thoroughly clean carburetor castings and metal parts
in an approved carburetor cleaner.

### CAUTION:
`chevrolet_camaro_en_753717df` | camaro | pdf_manual | tier:3 | lang:en | layer:general | p:171

Any rubber parts, plastic parts, dia­
phragms, pump plungers, electric parts and solen­
oids, should not be immersed in carburetor cleaner.
However, the air horn which has the pressure relief
valve will withstand normal cleaning in carburetor
cleaner. Make sure the cleaning solution is
thoroughly removed from pressure relief valve area.
2.

### Blow out all passages in castings with compressed air.
`chevrolet_camaro_en_dc8b9929` | camaro | pdf_manual | tier:3 | lang:en | layer:interior | p:171

Do not pass drills through jets or passages.
3.
Inspect idle mixture needle for damage.
4.
Examine float needle and seat assembly for wear. Install
a new factory matched set if worn.
Inspect upper and lower casting sealing surfaces for
damage.
