### Blow out bearings with compressed air.

### CAUTION: Do not allow the bearings to spin, but
`chevrolet_camaro_en_cf411036` | camaro | pdf_manual | tier:3 | lang:en | layer:general | p:243

Inspect all gears and replace all that are defective or

so equipped).
3.

### Make sure bearings are clean, then lubricate them with
`chevrolet_camaro_en_0d464de6` | camaro | pdf_manual | tier:3 | lang:en | layer:engine | p:243

light engine oil and check them for roughness. Rough­
ness may be determined by slowly turning the outer
race by hand.
CAUTION: Bearings must be lubricated with light
oil before checking for roughness.

### Bearing Rollers and Spacers
`chevrolet_camaro_en_459ed0d5` | camaro | pdf_manual | tier:3 | lang:en | layer:general | p:243

All main drive gear and countergear bearing rollers
should be inspected closely and replaced if they show wear.
Inspect countershaft at the same time and replace if neces­
sary. Replace all worn spacers.

### Fig. 8B--Removing Countershaft W ith J-22246
`chevrolet_camaro_en_aad41eff` | camaro | pdf_manual | tier:3 | lang:en | layer:general | p:243

Reverse Idler
1.
The bushings used in the idler gear are pressed into the
gear then peened into holes in the bores, and are bored
in place. This insures the positive alignment of the bush­
ings and their shafts, as well as proper meshing of gears.

### Because of the high degree of accuracy to which these
`chevrolet_camaro_en_7cb5e641` | camaro | pdf_manual | tier:3 | lang:en | layer:general | p:243

parts are machined, the bushings are not serviced sepa­
rately.
2.
Check bushings for excessive wear by using a narrow
feeler gauge between the shaft and the bushing or use
a micrometer. The proper clearance is from .003" to
.005".

REPAIRS
Reverse Shifter Shaft and Seal
Replacement
1.
With case extension removed from transmission the
reverse shifter shaft lock pin will already be removed.
(See Step 4 under Disassembly).
2.

### Remove shift fork.
`chevrolet_camaro_en_f7a77fd4` | camaro | pdf_manual | tier:3 | lang:en | layer:general | p:244

3. Carefully drive shifter shaft into case extension, allowing
ball detent to drop into case.
4. Place ball detent spring into detent spring hole and from
inside extension install shifter shaft fully into its opening
until the detent plate is butted against inside of extension
housing.
5.

### Place detent ball on spring (fig. 1 IB) and, holding ball
`chevrolet_camaro_en_fa156a8a` | camaro | pdf_manual | tier:3 | lang:en | layer:general | p:244

down with your thumb or a suitable tool push the
shifter shaft back in away from case until it is directly
over the ball and turn until the ball drops into detent
on the shaft detent plate.
6.
Install shift fork.

### NOTE: Do not drive the shifter shaft lock pin into
`chevrolet_camaro_en_77b50796` | camaro | pdf_manual | tier:3 | lang:en | layer:drivetrain | p:244

place until the extension has been installed on the
transmission case.
Extension Oil Seal Or Bushing
If bushing in rear of extension requires replacement,
remove oil seal and use Tool J-5778 to drive bushing into case
extension. Using the same tool, drive new bushing in from the
rear. Coat I.D. of bushing with transmission lubricant, then
install new oil seal using Tool J-5154. Prelubricate seal be­
tween lips with cup grease.

### Clutch Keys and Springs Replacement
`chevrolet_camaro_en_9c9f1b28` | camaro | pdf_manual | tier:3 | lang:en | layer:general | p:244

NOTE: The clutch hubs and sliding sleeves are a
select fit assembly and should be kept together as
originally assembled, but the three keys and two
springs may be replaced if worn or broken.
1.
Push the hub from the sliding sleeve. The keys will fall
free and the springs may be easily removed.
2.

### Place the two springs in position (one on each side of
`chevrolet_camaro_en_9e9642d5` | camaro | pdf_manual | tier:3 | lang:en | layer:general | p:244

the hub), so all three keys are engaged by both springs.
Place the keys in position and, holding them in place,
slide the hub into the sleeve.
NOTE: The sleeve with the large square edge oppo­
site the fork groove identifies the 3-4 synchronizer
sleeve.

### ASSEM BLY OF MAINSHAFT
`chevrolet_camaro_en_bd5e2e48` | camaro | pdf_manual | tier:3 | lang:en | layer:general | p:244

1.
From the rear of the mainshaft, assemble the secon
speed gear (with hub of gear toward rear of shaft).
2.
Install 1-2 synchronizer clutch assembly to mainshaft
(sliding clutch sleeve taper toward the rear, hub to the
front); together with a synchronizing ring on either side
of clutch assembly so their keyways line up with the
clutch keys (fig. 12B).
3.

### Press the 1st gear sleeve onto the mainshaft using a 1
`chevrolet_camaro_en_46fa8640` | camaro | pdf_manual | tier:3 | lang:en | layer:general | p:244

3/4" I.D. pipe cut to a convenient length or other suita­
ble tool.
4.
Install the first speed gear (with hub toward front) and
using 1 5/8" I.D. pipe cut to a suitable length, press on
the rear bearing (fig. 13B).
5.

### Choose the correct selective fit snap ring (.087", .090",
`chevrolet_camaro_en_4d981149` | camaro | pdf_manual | tier:3 | lang:en | layer:drivetrain | p:244

.093", or .096") and install it in the groove in mainshaft
behind the rear bearing. With proper ring, maximum
distance between snap ring and rear face of bearing will
be from zero to .005".
NOTE: Always use new snap rings when reassem­
bling transmission and do not expand the snap ring
further than is necessary for assembly.
6.

### Install the third speed gear (hub to front of transmis­
`chevrolet_camaro_en_470a3ee2` | camaro | pdf_manual | tier:3 | lang:en | layer:drivetrain | p:244

sion) and the third speed gear synchronizing ring (not­
ches to front of transmission).

7.
Install the third and fourth speed gear clutch assembly
(hub and sliding sleeve) with both sleeve taper and hub

ing ring.
8.

### Install snap ring in the groove in mainshaft in front of
`chevrolet_camaro_en_4deb6c51` | camaro | pdf_manual | tier:3 | lang:en | layer:interior | p:245

the third and fourth speed clutch assembly, with ends
of snap ring seated behind spline teeth.

rear bearing.
10.

### Install the reverse gear (shift collar to rear) and 2 anti­
`chevrolet_camaro_en_bddb1c2d` | camaro | pdf_manual | tier:3 | lang:en | layer:general | p:245

rattle springs (RPO M20 only).
11.
Install retaining clip and speedometer gear. On models
using the metal gear, press speed. Drive gear onto main­
shaft using a suitable press plate such as J-1453. Posi­
tion the gear to obtain a measurement of 4 7/8" from
the forward side of the gear to the flat surface of the rear
bearing retainer (Fig. 14B).

### ASSEM BLY OF COUNTERGEAR
`chevrolet_camaro_en_5dc36525` | camaro | pdf_manual | tier:3 | lang:en | layer:general | p:245

1.
Install roller spacer (tube type) in countergear.
2.
Using heavy grease to retain the rollers, install a spacer,
28 rollers, a spacer, 28 more rollers, then another
spacer. Install in the other end of the countergear, a
spacer, 28 rollers, a spacer, 28 more rollers, and another
spacer (fig. 15B).
3.

### Insert Tool J-22246 into countergear.
`chevrolet_camaro_en_f7c6709b` | camaro | pdf_manual | tier:3 | lang:en | layer:drivetrain | p:245

ASSEM BLY OF CASE COMPONENTS
1.
Rest the transmission case on its side with the side cover
opening toward the assembler. Put countergear tanged
thrust washers in place, retaining them with heavy
grease, making sure the tangs are resting in the notches
of the case.
2.

### Set countergear in place in bottom of transmission case,
`chevrolet_camaro_en_0717490d` | camaro | pdf_manual | tier:3 | lang:en | layer:drivetrain | p:245

making sure that tanged thrust washers are not
knocked out of place.
3.
Position the transmission case resting on its front face.
4.
Lubricate and insert countershaft in rear of case. Turn
countershaft so flat on end of shaft is horizontal and
facing bottom of case.
5.

### Align countergear with shaft in rear and hole in front
`chevrolet_camaro_en_823c1c3e` | camaro | pdf_manual | tier:3 | lang:en | layer:general | p:245

of case, and press countershaft into case (pushing as­
sembly tool out front of case) until flat on shaft is flush
with rear of case. Be sure thrust washers remain in place
(fig. 16B).
6.
Attach a dial indicator (fig. 17B) and check end plate
of the countergear. If end play is greater than .025" new
thrust washers must be installed.
7.

### Install cage and the seventeen roller bearings into main
`chevrolet_camaro_en_7871b6f0` | camaro | pdf_manual | tier:3 | lang:en | layer:drivetrain | p:245

drive gear, using heavy grease to hold the bearings in
place. Install oil slinger on main drive gear with con­
cave side toward gear.
8.
Install main drive gear and pilot bearings through the
side cover opening and into position in transmission
front bore.

retainer.
10.
Install the fourth speed synchronizing ring on main
drive gear with the notches toward the rear of the trans­
mission.
11.
Position the reverse idler gear thrust washer (tanged)
on the machined face of the ear cast in the case for the
reverse idler shaft and hold with heavy grease. Position
the front reverse idler gear next to the thrust washer,
with the hub facing toward rear of the case.

`chevrolet_camaro_en_e744959f` | camaro | pdf_manual | tier:3 | lang:en | layer:general | p:246

assembly to case, slide the 3-4 synchronizing clutch
sleeve forward into fourth speed detent position (fig.

ring correspond to the keys in the clutch assembly (fig.

### 18B).

CAUTION: Be sure main drive gear engages both
the countergear and antilash plate on standard ra­
tion models.
13.
With the guide pin in rear bearing retainer aligned with
hole in rear of case, tap rear bearing retainer into posi­
tion with a soft hammer.
14.

### From the rear of the case, insert the rear reverse idler
`chevrolet_camaro_en_6daf096e` | camaro | pdf_manual | tier:3 | lang:en | layer:general | p:246

gear, engaging the splines with the portion of the front
gear inside the case.
15.
Using heavy grease, place gasket in position on rear face
of rear bearing retainer.
16.
Install the remaining flat thrust washer on reverse idler
shaft. If new idler shaft is being used, drive out the roll
pin and press it into new shaft.
17.

### Install reverse idler shaft, roll pin, and thrust washer
`chevrolet_camaro_en_05d13445` | camaro | pdf_manual | tier:3 | lang:en | layer:drivetrain | p:246

into gears and front boss of case. Make sure to pick-up
front tanged thrust washer.
NOTE: Roll pin should be in a vertical position.
18.
Pull reverse shifter shaft to left side of extension and
rotate shaft to bring reverse shift fork forward in exten­
sion (reverse detent position). Start the extension onto
the transmission case (fig. 19B), while slowly pushing
in on the shifter shaft to engage the shift fork with the
reverse gear shift collar. Then pilot the reverse idler
shaft into the extension housing permitting the exten­
sion to slide onto the transmission case.
19.

### Install 6 extension and retainer-to-case attaching bolts.
`chevrolet_camaro_en_1df3edb8` | camaro | pdf_manual | tier:3 | lang:en | layer:general | p:246

Torque upper 3 bolts and lower 3 bolts to specification.
20.
Push or pull reverse shifter shaft to line up groove in the
shaft with the holes in the boss and drive in the lock pin.
Install shifter lever.
21.

### Press bearing onto main drive gear (snap ring groove to
`chevrolet_camaro_en_548c6604` | camaro | pdf_manual | tier:3 | lang:en | layer:interior | p:246

front) and into case until several main drive gear retain­
ing nut threads are exposed.
22.
Lock transmission up by shifting into two gears. Install
main drive gear retaining nut on the gear shaft and
draw it up tight using Tool J-0933. Be su~e bearing fully
seats against shoulder on gear. Torque retaining nut to
40 ft. lbs. and lock in place by staking securely into
S3

must be used to avoid damaging the threads on the
shaft.

`chevrolet_camaro_en_935b8c12` | camaro | pdf_manual | tier:3 | lang:en | layer:general | p:247

attaching bolts and (2) strip bolt lock retainers, using a

Shift mainshaft 3-4 sliding clutch sleeve into neutral
position and 1-2 sliding clutch sleeve into second gear
(forward) detent position. Shift side cover 3-4 shifter

### Install side cover gasket and carefully position side
`chevrolet_camaro_en_39d6f7d6` | camaro | pdf_manual | tier:3 | lang:en | layer:drivetrain | p:247

cover into plate. There is a dowel pin in the cover to
assure proper alignment with the case. Install attaching

of case.

### To remove bearing, position Tool J-22872 to the bear­

by hand and check for roughness.

using Tool J-22872 (fig. 1 IQ). Slinger should be located

8Q for direction of slinger installation.

5.
Check second speed thrust washer for excessive scoring.
6.
Inspect 2nd speed gear for excessive wear at thrust
surface. Check synchronizer springs for looseness or
breakage.
7.

### Inspect second gear synchronizing ring for excessive
`chevrolet_camaro_en_e75e114a` | camaro | pdf_manual | tier:3 | lang:en | layer:general | p:255

wear.
8.
Inspect bronze synchronizer cone on 2nd speed gear for
excessive wear or damage. Also inspect clutch gear syn­
chronizer cone and third speed gear synchronizer cone
for excessive wear or damage.

### NOTE: First and reverse sliding gear must be sliding
`chevrolet_camaro_en_396980ca` | camaro | pdf_manual | tier:3 | lang:en | layer:general | p:255

fit on synchronizer hub and must not have excessive
radial or circumferential play. If sliding gear is not
free on hub, inspect for burrs which may have rolled
up on front end of half-tooth internal splines and
remove by honing as necessary.
9.

### Inspect all gear teeth for excessive wear.
`chevrolet_camaro_en_e94216f7` | camaro | pdf_manual | tier:3 | lang:en | layer:general | p:255

Fig. 1 5Q--Disassembly of Mainshaft
1.
Remove first speed gear.
2.
Remove snap ring in front of 3rd-4th synchronizer as­
sembly.
3.
Remove reverse driven gear.
4.
Press behind second speed gear to remove 3rd-4th syn­
chronizer assembly, 3rd speed gear and 2nd speed gear
along with 3rd speed gear bushing and thrust washer
(fig. 15 Q).
5.

### Remove 2nd speed synchronizer ring.
`chevrolet_camaro_en_dfeddea5` | camaro | pdf_manual | tier:3 | lang:en | layer:general | p:255

6.
Remove 2nd speed synchronizer keys.
7.
Supporting 2nd speed synchronizer hub at front face,
press mainshaft through removing 1st speed gear bush­
ing and 2nd speed synchronizer hub.
8.
Split 2nd speed gear bushing with chisel and remove
bushing from shaft.

### CAUTION: Exercise care not to damage mainshaft.
`chevrolet_camaro_en_969202eb` | camaro | pdf_manual | tier:3 | lang:en | layer:general | p:255

Inspection
1.
Wash all parts in cleaning solvent.
2.
Inspect mainshaft for scoring or excessive wear at
thrust surfaces or splines.
3.
Inspect clutch hub and clutch sleeve for excessive wear
and make sure sleeve slides freely on clutch hub. Also
check fit of clutch hub on mainshaft splines.

### NOTE: Third and fourth speed clutch sleeve should
`chevrolet_camaro_en_983a772e` | camaro | pdf_manual | tier:3 | lang:en | layer:general | p:255

slide freely on third and fourth speed clutch hub but
clutch hub should be snug fit on shaft splines.
4.
Inspect 3rd speed gear thrust surfaces for excessive
scoring and inspect third speed gear mainshaft bushing
for excessive wear.

### NOTE: Third speed gear must be a running fit on
`chevrolet_camaro_en_c4807325` | camaro | pdf_manual | tier:3 | lang:en | layer:general | p:255

mainshaft bushing and mainshaft bushing should
be press fit on shaft.
Assembly
1.
Using Tool J-22873 press 2nd speed bushing onto main­
shaft until it bottoms against shoulder (fig. 16Q).
NOTE: Lubricate bushing with E.P. oil before press­
ing.

### CAUTION: 1 st, 2nd and 3rd speed gear bushings are
`chevrolet_camaro_en_f62f0783` | camaro | pdf_manual | tier:3 | lang:en | layer:general | p:255

sintered iron, exercise care when installing.
2.
Press 1st and 2nd speed synchronizer hub onto main­
shaft until it bottoms against shoulder with annulus
toward rear of shaft.

### Install new clutch countergear rear retaining ring using
`chevrolet_camaro_en_cba713c3` | camaro | pdf_manual | tier:3 | lang:en | layer:general | p:257

Tool J22830, J-22873 and snap ring pliers as follows:
Install Tool J-22830 on end of shaft and position snap

snap ring pliers, carefully expand ring until it just slides
onto splines, then push ring down shaft until it engages
groove on shaft.

DISASSEM BLY OF TRANSMISSION (Refer to
The following procedures cover complete overhaul of the
2.
transmission. The transmission should be overhauled in se­
quence described unless only one unit is to be worked on.
1.

### Mount transmission assembly in holding fixture; then
`chevrolet_camaro_en_bef56e3d` | camaro | pdf_manual | tier:3 | lang:en | layer:drivetrain | p:261

3.
if not previously removed, remove drain and filler
4.
plugs. Shift transmission into neutral position.
Figures 1K and 2K)
Remove eight screws and washers, and remove cover
from transmission case. Remove cover to case gasket
and discard.

### Lock transmission into two speeds at one time.
`chevrolet_camaro_en_0525034b` | camaro | pdf_manual | tier:3 | lang:en | layer:drivetrain | p:261

Remove four screws with lock washers and remove rear
bearing retainer and gasket from case. Discard gasket.
CHEVROLET OVERHAUL MANUAL
CLUTCHES AND TRANSMISSIONS 7-52
5.
Remove speedometer drive gear from rear end of main­
shaft.
6.

### Using a suitable puller over snap ring on bearing
`chevrolet_camaro_en_5bbbedda` | camaro | pdf_manual | tier:3 | lang:en | layer:drivetrain | p:262

remove mainshaft rear bearing.
7.
Remove four self-locking, self-sealing screws and
remove main drive gear retainer and gasket. Discard
gasket.
8.
Rotate main drive gear assembly so part of gear with
missing clutch teeth is on the bottom. Pull drive gear
assembly straight out of transmission.
9.

### Lift 3rd and 4th speed synchronizer parts out of case
`chevrolet_camaro_en_d21be992` | camaro | pdf_manual | tier:3 | lang:en | layer:drivetrain | p:262

(fig. 11K).
NOTE: On light duty models remove the roller type
thrust bearing on the mainshaft then slide synchro­
nizer parts from mainshaft.
10.
Lift mainshaft and gears assembly from transmission
case.
11.

### Remove screw and lock plate retaining reverse idler
`chevrolet_camaro_en_96fc3ec1` | camaro | pdf_manual | tier:3 | lang:en | layer:general | p:262

shaft.
12.
Using a suitable puller, pull reverse idler shaft from
case. Remove idler gear from inside case.
13.
Remove four screws and lock washers, then remove
countershaft rear bearing retainer and gasket. Discard
gasket.
14.

### Remove countershaft rear thrust bearing and race.
`chevrolet_camaro_en_23068fe2` | camaro | pdf_manual | tier:3 | lang:en | layer:drivetrain | p:262

15.
Lift countershaft gear out of transmission case.
16.
If so equipped, remove power take off cover attaching
screws and lock washers. Remove cover and gasket.
Discard gasket.
CLEANING AND INSPECTION
(Refer to Figure 2K)

### Cleaning
`chevrolet_camaro_en_36170b50` | camaro | pdf_manual | tier:3 | lang:en | layer:drivetrain | p:262

During overhaul procedures all components of the trans­
mission (except bearing assemblies) should be thoroughly
cleaned with cleaning solvent and dried with air pressure
prior to inspection and reassembly of the transmission.
1.

### Clean the bearing assemblies as follows:
`chevrolet_camaro_en_6eeade69` | camaro | pdf_manual | tier:3 | lang:en | layer:general | p:262

a.
Careful and proper cleaning of bearings is of utmost
importance. Bearings should always be cleaned
separately from other parts.
b.
Soak all bearing assemblies in CLEAN cleaning sol­
vent. Gasoline is not recommended. Bearings
should never be cleaned in hot solution tank.
c.

### Slush bearings in solvent until all old lubricant is
`chevrolet_camaro_en_1b9ec119` | camaro | pdf_manual | tier:3 | lang:en | layer:general | p:262

loosened. Hold bearing races so bearings will not
rotate; then brush bearings with a soft bristled brush
until ALL D IRT has been removed. Remove loose
particles of dirt by striking bearing flat against a
block of wood.
d.

### Rinse bearings in clean solvent; then blow bearings
`chevrolet_camaro_en_bf1abed5` | camaro | pdf_manual | tier:3 | lang:en | layer:general | p:262

dry with air pressure. DO NOT SPIN BEARINGS
W HILE DRYING.
e.
Rotate each bearing slowly while examining balls or
rollers for roughness, damage, or excessive wear.
Replace all bearings that are not in first class condi­
tion.

### NOTE: After cleaning and inspecting bearings as
`chevrolet_camaro_en_0a07fd4b` | camaro | pdf_manual | tier:3 | lang:en | layer:drivetrain | p:262

directed, lubricate bearings generously with lubri­
cant recommended in LUBRICATION (SEC. 0) of
this supplement; then wrap each bearing in clean
paper until ready to reinstall in transmission.
2.
Remove all portions of old gaskets from parts, using a
stiff brush or scraper.

### Inspection
`chevrolet_camaro_en_9cd10bad` | camaro | pdf_manual | tier:3 | lang:en | layer:general | p:262

1.
Inspect all parts for discoloration or warpage due to
heat.
2.
Examine all gear teeth and splines for chipped, worn,
broken, or nicked teeth or splines. Small nicks or burrs
may be removed with a fine abrasive stone.
3.

### Inspect the breather assembly to see that is open and
`chevrolet_camaro_en_e354fddb` | camaro | pdf_manual | tier:3 | lang:en | layer:general | p:262

not damaged.
4.
Check all threaded parts for damaged, stripped or
crossed threads.
5.
Replace all gaskets, oil seals, and snap rings.
6.
Examine housing, retainers, and covers for cracks or
other damage. Since repairs by welding, brazing, etc.,
are not recommended, replace damaged parts.
7.

### Check keys and keyways for condition and fit.
`chevrolet_camaro_en_13b85f94` | camaro | pdf_manual | tier:3 | lang:en | layer:general | p:262

8.
Inspect shift forks for wear, distortion, or other dam­
age.
9.
Check detent ball springs for distortion or collapsed
coils.
10.
Inspect thrust washers, stop rings, and spacers for wear
or damage.
11.

### Check fit of bearing on their respective shafts and in
`chevrolet_camaro_en_8f590599` | camaro | pdf_manual | tier:3 | lang:en | layer:general | p:262

their bores. Inspect bearings, shafts, and case for wear.
If installation of a new bearing does not correct condi­
tions, install new shafts or replace the case.
12.
Make sure synchronizer sliding clutch slides freely on
clutch gear. Check pins on synchronizer outer stop
rings for straightness and tightness.
13.

### Inspect all bearing rollers for pitting or galling.
`chevrolet_camaro_en_a3a23c5f` | camaro | pdf_manual | tier:3 | lang:en | layer:drivetrain | p:262

14.
Examine detent balls for corrosion or brinneling. If shift
lever shaft detents show signs of wear, replace them.
15.
Replace all worn or damaged parts. When reassembling
the transmission, coat all moving parts with lubricant
recommended in LUBRICATION (SEC.O) of the ap­
propriate Chevrolet Service Manual.

2nd shift lug.

With a No. 2 easy out remove roll pin from 1st and 2nd
shift fork.

### Using No. 2 easy out, remove roll pins from reverse

shift lug assembly and shift fork.

### Using a screw driver, remove retaining ring from re­

verse shift lug assembly. Remove washer, plunger and

A ssem bly (Fig. 3K)
1.
Position detent spring and ball in bore of cover.
2.
Partially insert 1st and 2nd speed shift rail into bore of
cover. Position 1st and 2nd speed shift fork and 1st and
2nd speed shift lug on rail.

### Push 1st and 2nd speed shift rail the remaining distance
`chevrolet_camaro_en_bbc328d5` | camaro | pdf_manual | tier:3 | lang:en | layer:general | p:264

(to neutral position) into cover and install new lock

5.

### Position detent spring and ball in bore of cover.

### Push 3rd and 4th shift rail the remaining distance into

`chevrolet_camaro_en_7ebece86` | camaro | pdf_manual | tier:3 | lang:en | layer:general | p:264

Install rail interlock hole plug.
Main Drive Gear
Disassembly (Fig. 5K and 6K)
1.
Remove mainshaft pilot bearing snap ring from cavity
at rear of main drive gear.
2.
Remove pilot bearing washer and 14 pilot bearing roll­
ers from drive gear.
3.

### Using snap ring pliers, remove drive gear bearing re­
`chevrolet_camaro_en_ab23be42` | camaro | pdf_manual | tier:3 | lang:en | layer:general | p:264

taining selective snap ring.
4.
Using bearing remover plates (J-8176), or other suitable
tool, press main drive gear gront bearing off drive gear
shaft.
5.
Remove drive gear bearing oil slinger from drive gear
shaft.

### Assembly
`chevrolet_camaro_en_2b197e08` | camaro | pdf_manual | tier:3 | lang:en | layer:general | p:264

1.
Position oil slinger, dished side down, on main driver
gear; then, using a suitable sleeve, press or drive front
bearing on shaft of gear.
2.
Using snap ring pliers; install front bearing selective
snap ring in groove of drive gear shaft.

### Using light grease to retain bearing rollers, position 14
`chevrolet_camaro_en_6cce3dcf` | camaro | pdf_manual | tier:3 | lang:en | layer:drivetrain | p:264

bearing rollers in cavity of main drive gear.
4.
Position thrust washer over bearing rollers; then using
a small screw driver, install snap ring in groove of drive
gear.

### Seal
`chevrolet_camaro_en_1a3edc55` | camaro | pdf_manual | tier:3 | lang:en | layer:general | p:265

Replacement
1.
Remove bearing retainer oil seal from main drive gear
bearing retainer.

Using a suitable sleeve, press or drive new oil seal into

NOTE: Lip of oil seal should point toward gasket
surface of retainer.

### Mainshaft
`chevrolet_camaro_en_bae4cd2a` | camaro | pdf_manual | tier:3 | lang:en | layer:general | p:265

Disassembly
1.
Remove mainshaft rear spacer from rear of mainshaft.
2.
Remove mainshaft 1st speed sliding gear from main­
shaft.
3.
Remove synchronizer clutch gear snap ring, then
remove synchronizer clutch gear.
4.

### Remove mainshaft 3rd speed gear and synchronizer
`chevrolet_camaro_en_64dcdbe9` | camaro | pdf_manual | tier:3 | lang:en | layer:general | p:265

adjusting shims if used.
5.
Remove mainshaft 2nd speed gear split ring.
6.
Remove mainshaft 2nd speed gear and synchronizer
assembly from mainshaft.
7.
Remove 2nd speed synchronizer retaining ring from
synchronizer pins. Remove synchronizer spring assem­
bly and synchronizer spring from 2nd speed gear.

### Assembly
`chevrolet_camaro_en_8040fbf1` | camaro | pdf_manual | tier:3 | lang:en | layer:general | p:265

1.
Position 2nd speed gear and synchronizer inner stop
ring and pin assembly on bench. Place synchronizer
spring in stop ring (fig. 7K).
2.
Place mainshaft 2nd speed gear over spring and ring.
3.
Install retaining snap ring, when tangs of snap ring
pointing out.
4.

### Position 2nd speed gear and synchronizer assembly on
`chevrolet_camaro_en_7bca3ae3` | camaro | pdf_manual | tier:3 | lang:en | layer:sensors | p:265

mainshaft.
5.
Install mainshaft 2nd speed gear split ring in groove of
mainshaft making sure ends of ring are securely lock
together (fig. 8K).
NOTE: Lubricate parts. Parts should turn freely.
6.
Position mainshaft 3rd speed gear on mainshaft and
lubricate freely. Gear should turn easily.
7.

### Install 3rd and 4th synchronizer sliding clutch gear on
`chevrolet_camaro_en_52491705` | camaro | pdf_manual | tier:3 | lang:en | layer:general | p:265

mainshaft.
8.
Using snap ring pliers, install mainshaft clutch gear
snap ring in groove of mainshaft.
NOTE: Install the thickest snap ring possible in
groove of shaft. Snap rings are available in four dif­
ferent thicknesses as shown in the following table:
T h in .......................................................... 0.086” - 0.088”
M edium .................................................... 0.089” - 0.091”
T hick.........................................................0.091” -0.094”
Extra Thick............................................ . 0.095” - 0.097”
9.

### Position mainshaft 1st speed sliding gear (51) on main­
`chevrolet_camaro_en_f45c97e9` | camaro | pdf_manual | tier:3 | lang:en | layer:drivetrain | p:265

shaft.

Countershaft Bearings
Replacement (Front or Rear)
1.
If inspection shows countershaft bearing needle rollers
are worn or damaged, remove rollers from retainer.

### Clean and inspect retainer, if not previously accom­
`chevrolet_camaro_en_9fcf646e` | camaro | pdf_manual | tier:3 | lang:en | layer:drivetrain | p:266

plished.
2.
Using a heavy grease to hold rollers in place, position
needle rollers in bore of bearing retainers.
Reverse Idler Gear Assembly
Two different design reverse idler gears are used in the
4-speed New Process transmission models on Chevrolet
trucks. All models use a bushing in the gear except for Tilt
Cab models (6.69 ratio) which use a reverse idler gear incor­
porating a heavy duty needle roller bearing assembly. Nei­
ther the bushing or roller bearing is serviced separately and
the gear and bearing must be replaced as an assembly.

Main Drive Gear
Installation
1.
With part of clutch gear with missing teeth down to
allow for passage over countershaft gear, guide main
drive gear assembly into transmission case and over
front end of mainshaft. Be sure front synchronizer stop
ring engages teeth of drive gear. Push the assembly in
until snap ring on bearing is against transmission case.
2.

### Position main drive gear bearing retainer (without gas­
`chevrolet_camaro_en_767085fc` | camaro | pdf_manual | tier:3 | lang:en | layer:drivetrain | p:269

ket), over drive gear shaft and against the transmission
case.
3.
While holding bearing retainer in place and using a
feeler gauge, check gap between retainer and transmis­
sion case. Remove bearing retainer; then reinstall bear­
ing retainer, two new gaskets and sufficient shims to
obtain a thick ness approximately .010-.015" greater
than previously measured.
4.

### Install four self-sealing, self-locking screws attaching
`chevrolet_camaro_en_4f26a307` | camaro | pdf_manual | tier:3 | lang:en | layer:drivetrain | p:269

drive gear bearing retainer to transmission case.
Tighten screws firmly (25-35 lb. ft.).
5.
Using a dial indicator, check end play of the input gear
(fig. 12K). If end play is not .007 to .017", remove or
add shims as required.

1.

bly is covered later in this section.

Shafts and Gears-Clean all shafts in cleaning solution to

### Case, Cover and Bearing Cups-Transfer case, cover, and
`chevrolet_camaro_en_2fa46011` | camaro | pdf_manual | tier:3 | lang:en | layer:general | p:272

bearing cups must be thoroughly cleaned in solution to
remove all accumulations of lubricant and dirt. Remove all
trace of gaskets from surfaces where used.
Inspection-Carefully inspect all bearings and rollers for
evidence of chipping, cracks, or worn spots that would render
bearing unfit for further service. Bearings are non-adjustable
and if worn or damaged, must be replaced with new parts.
Inspect shaft splines and gears. If any indication of failure,
such as chipped teeth or excessive wear is indicated, those
parts should be replaced with new parts.

### Assembly of Transfer Case
`chevrolet_camaro_en_1460df41` | camaro | pdf_manual | tier:3 | lang:en | layer:general | p:275

1.
Position front wheel drive shift fork in case and push
shift rail through case front. Align set screw hole in fork
with shaft hole and install set screw. Torque set screw
to 15 ft. lbs.
NOTE: Shift fork set screw boss should face front
of case.
2.

### Position rear wheel drive clutch gear and shift fork in
`chevrolet_camaro_en_4578531b` | camaro | pdf_manual | tier:3 | lang:en | layer:general | p:275

the case. Push shift rail through case front into fork and
case rear. Install set screw and torque to 15 ft. lbs.
NOTE: Gear shift collar should face to case rear.
3.
Place front wheel drive clutch in shift fork with collar
toward case rear.
4.

### Support front output shaft and press rear bearing onto
`chevrolet_camaro_en_a7dedf3b` | camaro | pdf_manual | tier:3 | lang:en | layer:interior | p:275

shaft using Tool J-6219 as shown in Figure 13D.
5.
Install front output shaft through rear of case into
clutch gear, drive gear and spacer. Position rear bearing
cup to case and tap to within 1/8 inch of seat.
6.

### Position front bearing on shaft. Supporting rear of
`chevrolet_camaro_en_59889f4b` | camaro | pdf_manual | tier:3 | lang:en | layer:general | p:275

shaft, press bearing into position using Tool J-6219 as
shown in Figure 14D. Tap front of shaft rearward to
repostion rear bearing cup.
Fig. 13D—Installing Front Output Shaft Rear Bearing
Fig. 1 4 D ~ ln s ta llin g  F ro n t O u tp u t S h a ft F ro n t B e a rin g
7.

### Slide spacer onto shaft. Position front bearing cup and
`chevrolet_camaro_en_11b8728a` | camaro | pdf_manual | tier:3 | lang:en | layer:general | p:275

tap into bore until flush with inner face.
8.
Install shim pack and rear cover. Torque bolts to 30 ft.
lbs.
9.
Position retainer gasket to case and start rails into front
bearing retainer.
NOTE: If shift rail seals were removed, position new
seals in retainer rail bores and press seals into place
using a block of wood or other suitable tool.
10.

### Install the poppet ball springs in the housing access
`chevrolet_camaro_en_a29d48d5` | camaro | pdf_manual | tier:3 | lang:en | layer:general | p:275

holes.
CAUTION: The longer spring (yellow) must be used
on the rear wheel drive rail and the shorter (red) on
the front wheel shift rail.
11.
Depress the poppet ball on the poppet spring for the
rear wheel drive and tap housing until end of rail passes
over the ball. Repeat with other rail.
12.

### Lubricate rail seals and carefully slide shift rails
`chevrolet_camaro_en_1c8f9745` | camaro | pdf_manual | tier:3 | lang:en | layer:general | p:275

through seals , then tap housing against case.
CAUTION: Seals may be damaged unless rails are
free of burrs or rough edges.
13.
Install front output shaft retainer bolts. Torque to 30 ft
lbs.
14.
Install front output shaft retainer seal using Tool J22833 as shown in Figure 15D.
15.

### If shift rail cups are damaged or have been removed,
`chevrolet_camaro_en_9c90577b` | camaro | pdf_manual | tier:3 | lang:en | layer:general | p:275

position new cup in case bore and install by tapping on
end of cup.
CAUTION: Distorted cups may permit leakage and
interfere with shift rail operation.
16.
Install front output shaft yoke, washer and locknut.

### Using dummy shaft J-23419, install needle bearings and
`chevrolet_camaro_en_105a3b55` | camaro | pdf_manual | tier:3 | lang:en | layer:general | p:276

spacers in intermediate gear. Position thrust washers in

### Install rear output shaft bearing assembly. Torque re­
`chevrolet_camaro_en_212e99fb` | camaro | pdf_manual | tier:3 | lang:en | layer:general | p:276

ings when engaging input shaft pilot.

### CAUTION: Rear yoke locknut must be torqued to
`chevrolet_camaro_en_dafbd14b` | camaro | pdf_manual | tier:3 | lang:en | layer:general | p:276

installing the rear prop shaft.
21.
Shift transfer gears. Check gear engagement and shift
rail movement. The four-wheel drive rail will have the

22.

### Position bottom cover and gasket to case. Install cover
`chevrolet_camaro_en_809df5b5` | camaro | pdf_manual | tier:3 | lang:en | layer:general | p:276

bolts and torque to 15 ft. lbs.
23.
After the complete rebuild of the parts, and bearing
retainer caps into unit, check the rear and front output
shafts end play for .001 to .005 inch. Add or remove
shims at the proper location on rear output bearing cap
taper bearing, and the front output rear bearing cover.

### To obtain proper specified end play, checking of the end
`chevrolet_camaro_en_6d34ab22` | camaro | pdf_manual | tier:3 | lang:en | layer:interior | p:276

play of shafts is important. It controls the seating of all
the taper bearings in the transfer case during the operat­
ion in the vehicle. Improper end play can shorten the
life of the taper bearings in the unit.

Bearings-Place all bearings and rollers in cleaning solu­
tion and allow to remain long enough to loosen all ac-

so that bearings do not spin.

### Shafts and Gears-Clean all shafts in cleaning solution to
`chevrolet_camaro_en_7a72e0a1` | camaro | pdf_manual | tier:3 | lang:en | layer:general | p:280

remove all accumulations. Dry with compressed air.
Case, Cover and Bearing Cups-Transfer case, cover, and
bearing cups must be thoroughly cleaned in solution to
remove all accumulation of lubricant and dirt. Remove all
trace of gaskets from surfaces where used.

### Inspection-Carefully inspect all bearings and rollers for
`chevrolet_camaro_en_18040bea` | camaro | pdf_manual | tier:3 | lang:en | layer:general | p:280

evidence of chipping, cracks, or worn spots that would render
bearing unfit for further service. Bearings are non-adjustable
and if worn or damaged, must be replaced with new parts.
Inspect shaft splines and gears. If any indication of failure,
such as chipped teeth or excessive wear, is indicated, those
parts should be replaced with new parts.

ously removed) using Tool J-9276-2 and Handle J-8092
(Fig. 10C).

Assemble the two bearing cones, spacer, shims and idler
gear on dummy shaft J-23429 with bore up. Check end
play (Fig. 11C). Limits are .000 to .002 inch.

### Install idler gear assembly with dummy shaft into case

### Install idler shaft cover and gasket. Torque bolts to 20

### Install interlock pins through large bore or P.T.O.

### Install input shaft bearing and shaft into case.

### Place front output shaft in soft jawed vise, spline end

down. Install front low gear over shaft with clutch gear
facing down and install thrust washer pin, thrust

opposite the pin.

### Position front wheel hi-gear and washer in case. Install

sliding clutch in the shift fork, then put fork and rail in

teeth in mesh with the teeth of the front wheel hi-gear.
4.
Line up washer, high gear, and sliding clutch with bear­
ing bore. Insert front output shaft and low gear assem­
bly through the high gear assembly.

### DISASSEM BLY OF TRANSMISSION
`chevrolet_camaro_en_ea0ef024` | camaro | pdf_manual | tier:3 | lang:en | layer:drivetrain | p:287

NOTE: The following overhaul procedures will also
apply to the Torque Drive transmission as well as to
the powerglide except where noted.
1.
Place transmission in Holding Fixture J-3289-01 and
Adapters J-9506 (fig. 2PG).

### NOTE: Cleanliness is an important factor in the
`chevrolet_camaro_en_8b1c4c9a` | camaro | pdf_manual | tier:3 | lang:en | layer:drivetrain | p:287

overhaul of the transmission. Before attempting any
disassembly operation, the exterior of the case
should be thoroughly cleaned to prevent the possi­
bility of dirt entering the transmission internal
mechanism. During disassembly, all parts should be
thoroughly cleaned in cleaning fluid and then air
dried. Wiping cloths or rags should not be used to
dry parts as lint may be deposited on the parts
which may cause later trouble.

### CAUTION: Do not use solvents which could damage
`chevrolet_camaro_en_03eb55f1` | camaro | pdf_manual | tier:3 | lang:en | layer:general | p:287

rubber seals or clutch plate facings.
2.
Remove converter holding tool previously installed and
remove converter assembly.
NOTE: When the overhaul is due to tranmission
clutch failure it is mandatory that the converter be
replaced.

### Extension, Governor and Governor
`chevrolet_camaro_en_3e58b781` | camaro | pdf_manual | tier:3 | lang:en | layer:drivetrain | p:287

Support (Powerglide)
3.
If replacement is necessary, remove speedometer driven
gear. Loosen capscrew and retainer clip holding speed­
ometer driven gear in extension and remove gear.
4.
Remove transmission extension by removing five bolts
retaining extension to case. Note seal ring on governor
support. (Pilot on Torque Drive.).
5.

### Remove the speedometer drive gear from output shaft
`chevrolet_camaro_en_e51ac9e1` | camaro | pdf_manual | tier:3 | lang:en | layer:general | p:287

as shown on Figure 3PG.
6.
Remove the "C" clip from the governor shaft on the
weight side of the governor, then remove the shaft and
governor valve from the opposite side of the governor
assembly (fig. 4PG) and the urethane washer.

7.
Loosen the governor drive screw and remove the gover­
nor assembly over the end of the output shaft (fig.

### 5PG).
`chevrolet_camaro_en_f489b954` | camaro | pdf_manual | tier:3 | lang:en | layer:body | p:290

8.
Remove the four bolts retaining the governor support
to the transmission case and remove the support body,
gasket and extension seal ring.
Transmission Internal Components
9.
Rotate the holding fixture until the front of the trans­
mission is pointing up and remove the seven oil pump
bolts. The bolt holes are offset to facilitate proper loca­
tion upon installation.
10.

### Remove the oil pump and stator shaft assembly and the
`chevrolet_camaro_en_b7f0ee8d` | camaro | pdf_manual | tier:3 | lang:en | layer:general | p:290

selective fit thrust washer using J-9539 (or two 3/8"-16
x 10" stove bolts) and the slide weights from Tool J6585 (fig. 6PG). Note the two threaded holes to mount
the pullers. Remove the ring seal and gasket.

### NOTE: The pump bolts have special sealing washers
`chevrolet_camaro_en_27301232` | camaro | pdf_manual | tier:3 | lang:en | layer:drivetrain | p:290

which must be in place upon installation.
11.
Release the tension on the low band adjustment, then,
with transmission horizontal, grasp the transmission
input shaft and carefully work it and the clutch assem­
bly out of the case (fig. 7PG). Use care so as not to lose
the low sun gear (splined) bushing from the input shaft.

### The low sun gear thrust washer will probably remain in
`chevrolet_camaro_en_16cca695` | camaro | pdf_manual | tier:3 | lang:en | layer:brakes | p:290

the planet carrier.
CAUTION: Use care so as not to damage the ma­
chined face on the front of the clutch drum.
12.
The low brake band and struts may now be removed.
Fig. 5PG~Removing Governor Assembly-Powerglide
13.

### Remove the planet carrier and the output shaft thrust
`chevrolet_camaro_en_e044dd4a` | camaro | pdf_manual | tier:3 | lang:en | layer:drivetrain | p:290

caged bearing from the front of the transmission.
14.
Remove the reverse ring gear if it did not come out with
the planet carrier.
15.
Using a large screw driver remove the reverse clutch
pack retainer ring and then lift out the reverse clutch
plates and the (waved) cushion spring.

### NOTE: If difficulty is experienced in getting the
`chevrolet_camaro_en_8aa1f8c8` | camaro | pdf_manual | tier:3 | lang:en | layer:general | p:290

snap ring past the shoulder on the reverse pack pres­
sure plate, a feeler gauge may be used as a guide.
16.
Install Tool J-9542 through the rear bore of the case
with the flat plate on the rear face of the case and turn
down the wing nut to compress the rear piston spring
retainer and springs, then remove the snap ring (fig.
8PG). Tool J-8039 may be used to remove the snap ring
if desired.
17.

### Remove Tool J-9542, the reverse piston spring retainer
`chevrolet_camaro_en_45533787` | camaro | pdf_manual | tier:3 | lang:en | layer:drivetrain | p:290

and the 17 piston return springs.
CHEVROLET OVERHAUL MANUAL

port in the rear of the transmission case as shown in

19.
Remove the three servo cover bolts, servo cover, piston
and spring.
Oil Pan and Valve Body
NOTE: The oil pan and valve body may be serviced
without the necessity of removing the extension
and internal components covered in the preceding
steps.
20.

### Rotate the holding fixture until the transmission is up­
`chevrolet_camaro_en_f37ec78a` | camaro | pdf_manual | tier:3 | lang:en | layer:drivetrain | p:291

side down and the oil pan is at the top. Remove the oil
pan attaching bolts, oil pan and gasket. Remove screen:
replace at assembly using new transmission case screen.
Fig. 7PG~Removing Clutch Drum and Input Shaft

### Fig. 8PG--Removing Rear Piston Spring Retainer Snap Ring
`chevrolet_camaro_en_78f43f02` | camaro | pdf_manual | tier:3 | lang:en | layer:body | p:291

21.
Remove the vacuum modulator and gasket, and the
vacuum modulator plunger, dampening spring (except
L-4 model) and valve (fig. 10PG).
22.
Remove the two bolts attaching the detent guide plate
to the valve body and the transmission case. Remove
the guide plate and the range selector detent roller
spring.
23.

### Remove the remaining valve body-to-transmission case
`chevrolet_camaro_en_fba143df` | camaro | pdf_manual | tier:3 | lang:en | layer:body | p:291

attaching bolts (indicated by arrows in Figure 11PG)
and carefully lift out the valve body and gasket, disenFig. 9PG -Applying Air to Remove Rear Piston

### This completes the entire transmission disassembly proce­
`chevrolet_camaro_en_f7110a5a` | camaro | pdf_manual | tier:3 | lang:en | layer:general | p:292

dure. Component parts disassembly and repair procedures
will be found in succeeding pages of this manual.
OVERHAULING UNIT ASSEM BLIES
Convertor and Stator
The converter is a welded assembly and no internal re­
pairs are possible. Check the seams for stress or breaks and
replace converter if necessary.

### Fig. 12PG-lnner Control Levers, Parking Pawl and Bracket

Oil Pump
Seal Replacement
If the pump seal requires replacement, remove the pump
from the transmission, pry out and replace the seal. (Drive
new seal into place, fully seated in counterbore using J-6839).

### Then, if no further work is required on the pump, reinstall
`chevrolet_camaro_en_2b2bce79` | camaro | pdf_manual | tier:3 | lang:en | layer:body | p:292

it in the case.
NOTE: Outer diameter of the seal should be coated
with non-hardening sealer prior to installation.
Disassembly
1.
Remove bolts attaching pump cover to body and
remove the cover.
2.
Remove pump gears from body.

### CAUTION: Do not drop or nick gears. These gears
`chevrolet_camaro_en_2dfb5df5` | camaro | pdf_manual | tier:3 | lang:en | layer:body | p:292

are not heat treated.
3.
Remove the rubber seal ring from the pump body.
NOTE: See Figure 14PG for a layout of pump parts.

1.
Wash all parts in cleaning solvent and blow out all oil
passages. DO NOT USE RAGS TO DRY PARTS.

seals.

CLUTCHES AND TRANSMISSIONS 7-86
2.
Inspect pump gears for nicks or damage.
3.
Inspect body and cover faces for nicks or scoring. In­
spect cover hub O.D. for nicks or burrs which might
damage clutch drum bushing journal.
4.

### Check for free operation of the priming valve and re­
`chevrolet_camaro_en_4dcdf802` | camaro | pdf_manual | tier:3 | lang:en | layer:body | p:296

place if necessary.
5.
Inspect body bushing for galling or scoring. Check
clearance between body bushing and converter pump
hub (fig. 16PG). Maximum clearance is .005". If the
bushing is damaged, the oil pump body should be re­
placed.
6.

### Inspect converter housing hub O.D. for nicks or burrs
`chevrolet_camaro_en_4fda3ead` | camaro | pdf_manual | tier:3 | lang:en | layer:body | p:296

### NOTE: Outer diameter of seal should be coated with
`chevrolet_camaro_en_09daa752` | camaro | pdf_manual | tier:3 | lang:en | layer:general | p:296

a non-hardening sealer prior to installation.
8.
On water cooled models so equipped, check condition
of oil cooler by-pass valve and replace if valve leaks
excessively. For removal, an "Easy Out" or its equiva­
lent may be used.

### For installation tap seat in place with soft hammer or
`chevrolet_camaro_en_7dae9466` | camaro | pdf_manual | tier:3 | lang:en | layer:body | p:296

brass drift so it is flush to .010" below the surface.
9.
With parts clean and dry, install pump gears and check:
a.
Clearance between O.D. of driven gear and body
should be .0035 "-.0065" (fig. 17PG).
b.

### Clearance between I.D. of driven gear and crescent
`chevrolet_camaro_en_597935ee` | camaro | pdf_manual | tier:3 | lang:en | layer:body | p:296

should be .003 "-.009" (fig. 18PG).
Fig. 1 7PG-Checking Driven Gear to Pump Body Clearance
c.
Gear end clearance (fig. 19PG) should be .0005"-
.0015".
Assembly
With the transmission facing up, proceed as follows:
1.

### Remove the input shaft, clutch drum, low band and
`chevrolet_camaro_en_49530c0b` | camaro | pdf_manual | tier:3 | lang:en | layer:drivetrain | p:296

struts as outlined uner "Transmission Disassembly."
2.
Install the downshift timing valve, conical end out, into
place in the pump cover to a height of 17/32" measured
from the shoulder of the valve assembly to face of pump
cover.

### Fig. 16PG~Checking Pump Body Bushing to Converter Pump
`chevrolet_camaro_en_3f8e0b6a` | camaro | pdf_manual | tier:3 | lang:en | layer:body | p:296

Hub Clearance
Fig. 18PG--Driven Gear to Crescent Clearance
CHEVROLET OVERHAUL MANUAL
CLUTCHES AND TRANSMISSIONS 7-87
Fig. 19PG~Checking Gear End Clearance
3.
Oil drive and driven gears generously and install in the
pump body.

### CAUTION: Assemble drive gear with recessed side
`chevrolet_camaro_en_2e7293d8` | camaro | pdf_manual | tier:3 | lang:en | layer:body | p:297

of the drive lugs downward-facing the converter.
4.
Carefully set the pump cover in place over the body and
loosely install 2 attaching bolts.
5.
Place the pump assembly, less the rubber seal ring,
upside down into the pump bore of the case (use guide
pins if desired). Install remaining attaching bolts and
torque to specification.
6.

### Remove pump assembly from case bore. Replace the
`chevrolet_camaro_en_7a2e4ad1` | camaro | pdf_manual | tier:3 | lang:en | layer:drivetrain | p:297

clutch drum and input shaft, low band and struts as
outlined under "Transmission Assembly."
NOTE: If necessary, remove two bolts and use J6585 pullers and J 6585-3 adapters to remove pump
assembly. Replace and retorque bolts.
7.

### Replace rubber seal ring in its groove in the pump body
`chevrolet_camaro_en_10a1cbec` | camaro | pdf_manual | tier:3 | lang:en | layer:general | p:297

and install the pump assembly properly in place in the
case bore, using a new gasket, being sure that the selec­
tive fit thrust washer is in place.
8.
Install the attaching bolts, using new bolt sealing wash­
ers if necessary.

### Governor Support Bushing Replacement
`chevrolet_camaro_en_2009dda3` | camaro | pdf_manual | tier:3 | lang:en | layer:general | p:297

If the governor support bushing must be replaced, it may
be removed using Tool J-9557 (and Handle J-7079) and rein­
stalled using Tool J-6582, pressing or driving the bushing in
from the front of the support.

### CLUTCH DRUM
`chevrolet_camaro_en_6210e952` | camaro | pdf_manual | tier:3 | lang:en | layer:general | p:297

Disassembly
CAUTION: When working with the clutch drum,
use extreme care that the machined face on the
front of the drum (fig. 20PG) not be scratched,
scored, nicked or otherwise damaged during any of
the following service operations. This machined

### Fig. 20PG--Removing Clutch Spring Retainer Snap Ring
`chevrolet_camaro_en_4eda436e` | camaro | pdf_manual | tier:3 | lang:en | layer:general | p:297

face must be protected whenever it must be brought
to bear on a press or tool of any sort.
1.
Remove retainer ring and low sun gear and clutch
flange assembly from the clutch drum.
2.
Remove the hub rear thrust washer.
3.

### Lift out the clutch hub, then remove the clutch pack
`chevrolet_camaro_en_269d26f0` | camaro | pdf_manual | tier:3 | lang:en | layer:general | p:297

and the hub front washer.
4.
Remove the spring retainer using J-9542 as shown in
Figure 20PG, or if using an arbor press, use J-5133 and
J-7782 adapter ring. Compress the springs far enough
to allow removal of the retainer snap ring; then, releas­
ing pressure on the springs, remove the retainer and the
springs.

### NOTE: When using J-9542, place a piece of cloth or
`chevrolet_camaro_en_501b5fd7` | camaro | pdf_manual | tier:3 | lang:en | layer:general | p:297

cardboard between the tool and the front side of the
clutch drum as protection for the machined face.
5.
Lift up on the piston with a twisting motion to remove
from the drum, then remove the inner and outer seals.

### Inspection
`chevrolet_camaro_en_b6d3291e` | camaro | pdf_manual | tier:3 | lang:en | layer:general | p:297

1.
Wash all parts in cleaning solvent (air dry).
CAUTION: Do not use rags to dry parts.
2.
Check drum bushing for scoring or excessive wear.
3.
Check the steel ball in the clutch drum that acts as a
relief valve. Be sure that it is free to move in the hole
and that the orifice leading to the front of the drum is
open. If the clutch relief valve check ball in the clutch
drum is loose enough to come out or not loose enough
to rattle, replace the clutch drum as an assembly. Re­

### CHEVROLET OVERHAUL MANUAL
`chevrolet_camaro_en_523d9659` | camaro | pdf_manual | tier:3 | lang:en | layer:drivetrain | p:297

CLUTCHES AND TRANSMISSIONS 7-88
placement or restaking of the ball should not be at­
tempted.
4.
Check fit of clutch flange in drum slots. There should
be no appreciable radial play between these two parts.

### Also check low sun gear for nicks or burrs and bushing
`chevrolet_camaro_en_a58440eb` | camaro | pdf_manual | tier:3 | lang:en | layer:general | p:298

for wear.
5.
Check clutch plates for burning and wear.
Bushing Replacem ent (Fig. 2 1 PG)
1.
Remove the old bushing with Tool J-9546 using care
not to damage the bushing bore or the machined face
on the front of the clutch drum.
2.

### Use the same tool to install the new bushing. Press (do
`chevrolet_camaro_en_0cd3ac99` | camaro | pdf_manual | tier:3 | lang:en | layer:general | p:298

not hammer) the bushing into the clutch drum from the
machined face side of clutch drum. Press only far
enough so that the tool meets the clutch drum. Do not
force the tool against the clutch drum machined face.

### A ssem bly
`chevrolet_camaro_en_1db61536` | camaro | pdf_manual | tier:3 | lang:en | layer:drivetrain | p:298

1.
Install new piston inner seal in hub of clutch drum with
seal lip downward (toward front of transmission).
2.
Install a new piston seal in clutch piston. Seal lips must
be pointed toward the clutch drum (front of transmis­
sion). Lubricate seals generously and install piston in
clutch drum with a twisting motion.
3.

### Place the springs in position on the piston, then place
`chevrolet_camaro_en_340e3bc0` | camaro | pdf_manual | tier:3 | lang:en | layer:general | p:298

the retainer in place on the springs.
4.
Using Tools J-5133 and J-7782 and a press, or J-9542
as a hand operation, depress the retainer plate and
springs far enough to allow installation of the spring
retainer snap ring in its groove on the clutch drum hub.
5.

### Install the hub front washer with its lip toward the the
`chevrolet_camaro_en_1e98dd1d` | camaro | pdf_manual | tier:3 | lang:en | layer:general | p:298

clutch drum, then install the clutch hub.
6.
Install (wave) cushion spring wherever used, see chart.
measure this stack height. Now refer to chart and
select the proper selective driven plate and install it
into clutch drum on top of the cushion spring.
7.

### Install the steel reaction plates and faced drive plates
`chevrolet_camaro_en_842630ab` | camaro | pdf_manual | tier:3 | lang:en | layer:sensors | p:298

alternately, beginning with a steel reaction plate (fig.
22PG). See clutch chart.
8.
Install the rear hub thrust washer with its flange toward
the low sun gear, then install the low sun gear and
flange assembly and secure with retainer ring. When
installed, the openings in the retainer ring should be
adjacent to one of the lands of the clutch drum.
9.

### Check the assembly by turning the clutch hub to be sure
`chevrolet_camaro_en_b8c60f9f` | camaro | pdf_manual | tier:3 | lang:en | layer:brakes | p:298

it is free to rotate.
LOW BAND
The brake band used in the aluminum Powerglide trans­
mission has bonded linings which, due to the transmission
characteristics and band usage, should require very little at­
tention. However, whenever a transmission is disassembled
the band should be cleaned of metal particles and inspected.
1.

### Check lining for evidence of scoring or burning.
`chevrolet_camaro_en_3ad27365` | camaro | pdf_manual | tier:3 | lang:en | layer:general | p:298

2.
Check band and lining for cracks.
3.
Check all band linkage for excessive wear.

2.
Inspect planet pinions for nicks or other tooth damage.
3.
Check end clearance of planet gears. This clearance
should be .006" - .030" (fig. 23PG)
4.

### Check input sun gear for tooth damage, also check
`chevrolet_camaro_en_a6d02823` | camaro | pdf_manual | tier:3 | lang:en | layer:general | p:299

input sun gear rear thrust washer for damage.
5.
Inspect output shaft bearing surface for nicks or scoring
and inspect input pilot bushing.
6.
Inspect input shaft splines for nicks or damage and
check fit in clutch hub and input sun gear. Also check
fit of splines in turbine hub.
7.

### Check oil seal rings for damage; rings must be free in
`chevrolet_camaro_en_a9c26347` | camaro | pdf_manual | tier:3 | lang:en | layer:general | p:299

input shaft ring grooves. Remove rings and insert in
stator support bore and check to see that hooked ring
ends have clearance. Replace rings on shaft.
Repairs
NOTE: The large planet carrier assembly now has
the pinion shafts flared at each end for retention
into the carrier. No overhaul of the large planet car­
rier assembly should be attempted.

### Fig. 23PG-Checking Planet Gear End Clearance
`chevrolet_camaro_en_9ef0b1b2` | camaro | pdf_manual | tier:3 | lang:en | layer:general | p:299

Small Planet Carrier Assemb/y-Overhaul
If during inspection, the planet pinions, pinion needle
bearing, pinion thrust washers, input sun gear, and/or input
sun gear thrust washer should show evidenece of excessive
wear or damage, they should be replaced by using the follow­
ing procedure:

### Refer to Figure 24PG.
`chevrolet_camaro_en_08a8217f` | camaro | pdf_manual | tier:3 | lang:en | layer:general | p:299

1.
Place the planet carrier assembly in a fixture or vise so
that the front (parking lock gear, end) of the assembly
faces up.
2.
Using prick punches or other similar means, mark each
pinion shaft and also the planet carrier assembly (fig.
25PG), so that reassembling, each pinion shaft will be
reinstalled in the same location from which it was
removed.

### NOTE: The pinion shafts are not selectively fit but
`chevrolet_camaro_en_1df197d1` | camaro | pdf_manual | tier:3 | lang:en | layer:general | p:299

it is good practice to reinstall them in their original
locations.
3.
Remove the pinion shaft lock plate screws and rotate
the lock plate counter-clockwise sufficiently to remove
it.
4.
Starting with a short planet pinion, and using a soft
steel drift drive on the lower end of the pinion shaft
until the pinion shaft is raised above the press fit area
of the output shaft flange. Feed J-4599 into the short
planet pinion from the lower end, pushing the planet
pinion shaft ahead of it until the tool is centered in the
pinion and the pinion shaft is removed from the assem­
bly.

5.
Remove the short planet pinion from the assembly.
6.
Remove J-4599, needle bearings and needle bearing
spacers (3) from short planet pinion.

### CAUTION: Use care so as not to lose any of the
`chevrolet_camaro_en_fb8bc044` | camaro | pdf_manual | tier:3 | lang:en | layer:general | p:300

planet pinion needle bearings. Twently needle bear­
ings are used in each end and are separated by a
bearing spacer in the center.
7.
By following the procedure as outlined in Steps 4, 5 and
6, remove the adjacent long planet pinion that was
paired by thrust washers to the short planet pinion now
removed.

### NOTE: Twenty needle bearings are used in each end
`chevrolet_camaro_en_54e491a7` | camaro | pdf_manual | tier:3 | lang:en | layer:general | p:300

of the long pinion separated by a bearing spacer in
the center.
8.
Remove the upper and lower thrust washer.
9.
Remove and disassemble the remaining planet pinions,
in pairs, by first removing a short planet pinion and
then the adjacent long planet pinion.
10.

### Remove low sun gear needle thrust bearing, input sun
`chevrolet_camaro_en_8fae3153` | camaro | pdf_manual | tier:3 | lang:en | layer:general | p:300

gear and input sun gear thrust washer.
Bearing
NOTE: Planet pinion remover and replacer Tool J4599, comes in two pieces, both alike. Only one is
used when removing the planet pinion; two, how­
ever, must be used when reassembling.

### Fig. 25PG~Suggested Pinion Shaft Markings
`chevrolet_camaro_en_0e087856` | camaro | pdf_manual | tier:3 | lang:en | layer:drivetrain | p:300

CHEVROLET OVERHAUL MANUAL
CLUTCHES AND TRANSMISSIONS 7-91
11.
Wash all parts in cleaning solvent and air dry.
12.
Recheck the planet pinion gears and input sun gear for
nicks or other tooth damage; also check the planet pin­
ion thrust washer and input sun gear thrust washer.

### Check low sun gear needle thrust bearing for spalled
`chevrolet_camaro_en_0864c902` | camaro | pdf_manual | tier:3 | lang:en | layer:general | p:301

needles. Replace worn or damaged parts.
13.
Inspect the planet pinion needle bearings closely and if
there is indication of excessive wear, all the needle bear­
ings must be replaced. Also inspect pinion shafts closely
and, if worn, replace the worn shafts.
14.

### Inspect the input shaft bushing installed in the base of
`chevrolet_camaro_en_78978dea` | camaro | pdf_manual | tier:3 | lang:en | layer:general | p:301

the output shaft. If damaged, it may be removed by
threading Tool J 9534 into the bushing and pulling the
bushing out using Slide Hammer J-6585. New bearing
can be installed by pressing in flush or below thrust
surface with the pilot end of input shaft as press tool.
15.

### Using J-4599, assemble needle bearing spacer and nee­
`chevrolet_camaro_en_c08f3d99` | camaro | pdf_manual | tier:3 | lang:en | layer:general | p:301

dle bearings (20 in each path) in one of the long planet
pinions (fig. 24PG). Use petroleum jelly to aid in assem­
bling and holding the needle bearings in position.
16.
Position the long planet pinion with J-4599, centered in
the pinion assembly and with thrust washers at each
end, in the planet carrier. Oil grooves on thrust washers
must be toward gears.

### NOTE: The long planet pinions are located opposite
`chevrolet_camaro_en_ebe243b5` | camaro | pdf_manual | tier:3 | lang:en | layer:general | p:301

the ciosed portions of the carrier, while the short
planet pinions are located in the openings.
17.
Feed the second J-4599 in from the top picking up the
upper thrust washer and the planet pinion and pushing
the already installed Tool J-4599 out the lower end. As
the first tool is pushed down, check that it picks up the
lower thrust washer.
18.

### Select the proper pinion shaft, as marked in Step 2,
`chevrolet_camaro_en_76408b9f` | camaro | pdf_manual | tier:3 | lang:en | layer:general | p:301

lubricate the shaft and install it from the top, pushing
the assembling tools ahead of it.
19.
Turn the pinion shaft so that the slot or groove at the
upper end faces the center of the assembly.
20.
With a brass or soft steel drift, drive the pinion shaft in
until the lower end is flush with the lower face of the
planet carrier.
21.

### Following the same general procedure as outlined in
`chevrolet_camaro_en_b5e81749` | camaro | pdf_manual | tier:3 | lang:en | layer:general | p:301

Steps 15 through 20, assemble and install a short planet
pinion in the planet carrier adjacent to the long planet
pinion now installed.
NOTE: The thrust washers already installed with
the long planet pinion also suffice for this short pla­
net pinion as the two pinions are paired together on
one set of thrust washers.
22.

### Install the input sun gear thrust washer, the input sun
`chevrolet_camaro_en_8553ad36` | camaro | pdf_manual | tier:3 | lang:en | layer:general | p:301

gear and low sun gear needle thrust bearing.
23.
Assemble and install the remaining planet pinions, in
pairs, by first installing the long planet pinion and then
the adjacent short planet pinion.
24.
Check end clearance of planet gears. This clearance
should be .005" - .030" (fig. 23PG).
25.

### Place the pinion shaft lock plate in position, then with
`chevrolet_camaro_en_3b4374b3` | camaro | pdf_manual | tier:3 | lang:en | layer:general | p:301

the extended portions of the lock plate aligned with
slots in the planet pinion shafts, rotate the lock plate
clockwise until the three attaching screw holes are ac­
cessible.
26.
Install the pinion shaft lock plate attaching screws and
tighten to specification.

### GOVERNOR--POWERGLIDE
`chevrolet_camaro_en_db3899e4` | camaro | pdf_manual | tier:3 | lang:en | layer:body | p:301

The governor assembly is a factory balanced unit. If body
replacement is necessary, the two sections must be replaced
as a unit. Remove the governor as outlined under "Transmis­
sionDisassembly".
Disassembly

### NOTE: The governor valve and shaft were already
`chevrolet_camaro_en_e3020f4f` | camaro | pdf_manual | tier:3 | lang:en | layer:body | p:301

disassembled from the assembly during the removal
procedures.
1.
Remove the outer weight assembly by sliding toward
center of body.
2.
Remove the smaller inner weight retaining snap ring
and remove the inner weight and spring.
3.

### If it is considered necessary, remove the four body as­
`chevrolet_camaro_en_e1063371` | camaro | pdf_manual | tier:3 | lang:en | layer:body | p:301

sembly bolts and separate the body, hub and gasket.
Remove the two seal rings.
Inspection
Clean all parts thoroughly in a solvent and air dry. Check
condition of all component parts of the assembly. Replace
any bent, damaged or scored parts. Body and hub must be
replaced as a unit.

### Assembly
`chevrolet_camaro_en_36a338a1` | camaro | pdf_manual | tier:3 | lang:en | layer:body | p:301

1.
Reassemble governor weights and reinstall in body
bore. Replace seal rings on hub.
2.
Slide hub into place on output shaft and lock into place
with the drive screw. Install gasket and governor body
over output shaft, install governor shaft, line up prop­
erly with output shaft and install body attaching bolts.

### Torque to specification.
`chevrolet_camaro_en_d21f022c` | camaro | pdf_manual | tier:3 | lang:en | layer:body | p:301

NOTE: Place transmission selector lever in PARK to
keep shaft from turning while tightening these
bolts.
3.
Check the governor weight for free fit in body after the
four attaching bolts are torqued. If the weight sticks or
binds, loosen the bolts and retorque.

### Pressure Regulator Valve-Remove the snap ring,
`chevrolet_camaro_en_1175f597` | camaro | pdf_manual | tier:3 | lang:en | layer:body | p:303

then tilt valve body to remove the hydraulic
modulator valve sleeve and valve, pressure regulator
valve spring retainer, spring and pressure regulator
valve assembly.
Inspection
Since most valve failures are caused initially by dirt or
other foreign material preventing a valve from functioning
properly, a thorough cleaning of all parts in clean solvent is
mandatory. Check all valves and their bores for burrs or
other deformities which could result in valve hang-up.

`chevrolet_camaro_en_5e326632` | camaro | pdf_manual | tier:3 | lang:en | layer:body | p:303

ing the disassembly procedures given above and check­
ing Figure 27PG, if necessary.
NOTE: Upper and lower valve body gaskets are the
same.
2.
Carefully install the lower valve body and gasket and
install 15 1-3/8" attaching bolts. Torque to specifica­
tion.

`chevrolet_camaro_en_5f63f5aa` | camaro | pdf_manual | tier:3 | lang:en | layer:body | p:303

Install the valve body onto the transmission as outlined
under Transmission-Assembly.
VACUUM MODULATOR--POWERGLIDE
The vacuum modulator is mounted on the left rear of the
transmission and can be serviced from beneath the vehicle.

### Removal
`chevrolet_camaro_en_ed96f2fa` | camaro | pdf_manual | tier:3 | lang:en | layer:drivetrain | p:303

1.
Remove the vacuum line at the vacuum modulator.
2.
Unscrew the vacuum modulator from the transmission
using J-9543, if available, or any thin 1" tappet type
wrench.
3.
Remove the vacuum modulator plunger, dampening
spring (except L4 model) and valve (fig. 10PG) from
the transmission case.

### Inspection and Repairs
`chevrolet_camaro_en_74e5ca2a` | camaro | pdf_manual | tier:3 | lang:en | layer:drivetrain | p:303

Check the vacuum modulator plunger and valve for nicks
and burrs. If such cannot be repaired with a slip stone, re­
place the part.
The vacuum modulator can be checked with a vacuum
source for leakage. However, leakage normally results in
transmission oil pull-over and results in oil smoky exhaust
and continually low transmission oil. No vacuum modulator
repairs are possible; replace as an assembly.

### Installation
`chevrolet_camaro_en_38d957a4` | camaro | pdf_manual | tier:3 | lang:en | layer:brakes | p:303

1.
Install vacuum modulator valve, dampening spring (ex­
cept L4 model) and plunger in bore of transmission.
2.
Place a new gasket on vacuum modulator. The gasket
has centering tabs to hold it centered during installa­
tion.
3.

### Install vacuum modulator, tighten firmly, and install
`chevrolet_camaro_en_bafee438` | camaro | pdf_manual | tier:3 | lang:en | layer:drivetrain | p:303

vacuum line as follows (fig. 10PG): Rubber tubing "A"
should bottom against modulator can. Pipe assembly
"B" should bottom against the modulator extension.
TRANSMISSION CASE
Inspection
1.
Wash case thoroughly with cleaning solvent, air dry
and blow out all oil passages.

### CAUTION: Do not use rags to dry parts.
`chevrolet_camaro_en_5dfe0361` | camaro | pdf_manual | tier:3 | lang:en | layer:general | p:303

2.
Inspect case for cracks which may contribute to leak­
age.
3.
Inspect case rear bushing for damage or excessive wear.
NOTE: This is a precision bushing and if damaged or
worn excessively must be replaced.
4.

### Check shifter shaft seal. If it shows signs of damage or
`chevrolet_camaro_en_87017d8e` | camaro | pdf_manual | tier:3 | lang:en | layer:interior | p:303

leaking, pry it out and install a new seal. The new seal
must be firmly seated in case counterbore.
Repairs
Rear Bushing-Replacement
Transmission case rear bushing is a precision bushing
which requires no reaming or finishing after assembly.
1.

### Remove bushing by driving or pressing from within
`chevrolet_camaro_en_eb06473e` | camaro | pdf_manual | tier:3 | lang:en | layer:general | p:303

case using J-9557 and Handle J-7079.
2.
To install new bushing, drive or press bushing into
place from rear of case using Tool J-9557 and Handle
J-7079 (fig. 28PG).
CAUTION: Install bushing only until shoulder of J9557 contacts the rear face of the case. Excessive
force, either hammering or pressing may crack or
otherwise damage the aluminum case.

Wash extension thoroughly with cleaning solvent and
air dry.

NOTE: Use only transmission oil or petroleum jelly
as lubricants to retain bearings or races during as­
sembly. Lubricate all bearings, seal rings and clutch
plates prior to assembly.

### If removed, assemble manual linkage to case as described
`chevrolet_camaro_en_45ae63d2` | camaro | pdf_manual | tier:3 | lang:en | layer:general | p:305

in Step 1-7.
1.
Install the parking lock pawl and shaft and insert a new
"E" ring retainer.
2.
Install the parking lock pawl pull-back spring over its
boss to the rear of the pawl. The short leg of the spring
should locate in the hole in the parking pawl.
3.

### Install the parking lock pawl reaction bracket with its
`chevrolet_camaro_en_c0e338cd` | camaro | pdf_manual | tier:3 | lang:en | layer:general | p:305

two bolts.
4.
Fit the actuator assembly between the parking lock
pawl and the bracket.
5.
Insert the outer shift lever into the case, being careful
of the shaft seal, and pick up the inner shift lever and
parking lock assembly and tighten alien head screw.

### Lubricate the shaft and seal with oil.
`chevrolet_camaro_en_5eabd56f` | camaro | pdf_manual | tier:3 | lang:en | layer:general | p:305

6.
Insert outer TV lever and shaft, special washer and "O"
ring into case and pick up inner TV lever. Tighten alien
head nut.
NOTE: To prevent possible binding between throttle
and range selector controls; .010 to .020"clearance
must exist between inner TV lever and inner shift
lever after assembly.
7.

### Thread the low band adjusting screw into case.

NOTE: The above internal components are shown in

8.
Install the inner and outer seals on the reverse piston
and, lubricating the piston and case with transmission
oil, install the piston into the case (fig. 29PG). If neces­
sary, carefully slide a feeler gauge around the outer
diameter of the piston to start the seal ring into the bore.
9.

### With the support fixture turned so that the transmis­
`chevrolet_camaro_en_8af55c30` | camaro | pdf_manual | tier:3 | lang:en | layer:general | p:305

sion case is facing up, install the 17 reverse piston return
springs and their retainer ring.

through the rear bore of the case. With the flat plate on
the rear face of the case, turn down on the wing nut to
compress the return springs and allow the retaining ring
snap ring to be installed. Remove Tool J-9542.

### Install the large (waved) cushion spring.

12.
Lubricate and install the reverse clutch pack (fig.
30PG) beginning with a reaction (spacer) plate and
alternating with the drive plates (faced) until all reac­
tion plates and all drive plates are in place. The nutched
lug on each reaction plate is installed in the groove at
the 7 o’clock position in the case. Then install the thick
pressure plate which has a "dimple" in one lug to align
with the same slot in the case as the notched lugs on the
other reaction plates.

### All models have 4 reaction and 4 drive plates except truck
`chevrolet_camaro_en_5a9f14b3` | camaro | pdf_manual | tier:3 | lang:en | layer:engine | p:306

models with V8 engines which have 5 reaction and 5 drive
plates.

Install the clutch plate retaining ring.
14.
With the rear of the transmission case downward, align
the internal lands and grooves of the reverse clutch
pack faced plates, then engage the reverse ring gear with
these plates. This engagement must be made by "feel"
while jiggling and turning the ring gear.
15.

`chevrolet_camaro_en_19ecad45` | camaro | pdf_manual | tier:3 | lang:en | layer:drivetrain | p:306

shaft and install the planetary carrier and output shaft
into the transmission case (fig. 3IPG).

Move the transmission into a horizontal position. The
two input shaft seal rings should be in place on the
shaft. Install the clutch drum (machined face first) onto
the input shaft and install the low sun gear bushing
(splined) against shoulder on shaft.

### Install clutch drum and input shaft assembly into case,

ing low sun gear with the short pinions on the planet
carrier.

and, using guide studs from J-3387 set, install clutch
drum selective thrust washer, oil pump gasket and oil
pump to case. Install two pump-tocase bolts.

change to a thicker or thinner selective fit thrust

### LOW BAND ADJUSTM ENT
`chevrolet_camaro_en_45319c67` | camaro | pdf_manual | tier:3 | lang:en | layer:general | p:308

Tighten the low servo adjusting screw to 70 inch lbs. using
torque wrench, J-5853 and a 7/32" hex head driver (fig.
35PG) or J21848. The input and output shaft must be
rotated simultaneously to properly center the low band on
the clutch drum. Then back off four (4) complete turns for
a band which has been in use for 6,000 miles or more, or 3
turns for one in use less than 6,000 miles. Tighten the locknut
to specified torque.
psi, backoff the jam nut one (1) full turn. This increases the
dimension from the jam nut to the throttle valve assembly
stop. Conversely, tightening the jam nut one (1) full turn
lowers TV pressure 3 psi. A difference of 3 psi on TV pressure
will cause a change of approximately 2 to 3 M PH in the wide
open throttle upshift point. Smaller pressure adjustments can
be made by partial turns of the jam nut. The end of TV,
adjusting screw has an alien head so the screw may be held
stationary while the jam nut is moved.

### Valve Body Disassembly, Inspection, and
`chevrolet_camaro_en_21f6e0f3` | camaro | pdf_manual | tier:3 | lang:en | layer:body | p:325

Reassembly (fig. 55M)
Disassembly
1.
Position valve body assembly with cored face up and
direct clutch accumulator piston pocket positioned as
shown in Figure 55M.
2.
Remove manual valve from lower left hand bore.
3.

### From lower right hand bore remove the pressure
`chevrolet_camaro_en_3b8d1926` | camaro | pdf_manual | tier:3 | lang:en | layer:general | p:325

regulator valve train retaining pin, boost valve sleeve,
intermediate boost valve, reverse and modulator boost
valve, pressure regulator valve spring, and the pressure
regulator valve.
4.
From the next bore, remove the 2-3 shift valve train
retaining pin, sleeve, control valve spring, 2-3 shift con­
trol valve, shift valve spring, and the 2-3 shift valve.
5.

### From the next bore, remove the 1-2 shift valve train
`chevrolet_camaro_en_b2d6867b` | camaro | pdf_manual | tier:3 | lang:en | layer:general | p:325

retaining pin, sleeve, shift control valve spring, 1-2 shift
control valve, and the 1-2 shift valve.
6.
From the next bore, remove retaining pin, plug, manual
low control valve spring, and the manual low control
valve.
7.

### From the next bore, remove the retaining pin, spring,
`chevrolet_camaro_en_747c6d21` | camaro | pdf_manual | tier:3 | lang:en | layer:interior | p:325

seat, and the detent regulator valve.
8.
Install Tool J-21885, on direct clutch accumulator piston
and remove retaining "E" ring (fig. 56M).
9.
Remove direct clutch accumulator piston, and metal oil
seal ring, and spring.
10.

### From the next bore down from the direct clutch ac­
`chevrolet_camaro_en_6ceb2c69` | camaro | pdf_manual | tier:3 | lang:en | layer:interior | p:325

cumulator, remove the detent actuating lever bracket
bolt, bracket, actuating lever and retaining pin, stop,
spring retainer, seat, outer spring, inner spring, washer
and detent valve.
Inspection
1.
Inspect all valves for scoring, cracks and free movement
in their respective bores.
2.

### Inspect valve body for cracks, scored bores, intercon­
`chevrolet_camaro_en_fb8c5b2b` | camaro | pdf_manual | tier:3 | lang:en | layer:body | p:325

nected oil passages and flatness of mounting face.
3.
Check all springs for distortion or collapsed coils.
Reassembly
1.
Install direct clutch accumulator piston spring and pis­
ton into valve body.
2.

### Install special tool J-21885, and compress spring and
`chevrolet_camaro_en_f27c0447` | camaro | pdf_manual | tier:3 | lang:en | layer:interior | p:325

piston and secure with retaining ring.
NOTE: Align piston and oil seal ring when entering
bore.
3.
Install the detent valve, washer, outer spring, inner
spring, spring seat, and spring retainer. Install detent
valve stop and detent valve actuating bracket. Torque
bolt to 52 in. lbs. Assemble detent actuating lever with
retaining pin.
4.

### Install the pressure regulator valve, spring, reverse and
`chevrolet_camaro_en_547dd9b9` | camaro | pdf_manual | tier:3 | lang:en | layer:general | p:325

modulator boost valve, intermediate boost valve, boost
valve sleeve and retaining pin.
5.
In the next bore up, install 2-3 shift control valve, shift
control valve spring, 2-3 shift control valve, shift con­
trol valve spring, shift control valve sleeve and retaining
pin.
6.

### In the next bore up, install the 1-2 shift valve, 1-2 shift
`chevrolet_camaro_en_beb88ffb` | camaro | pdf_manual | tier:3 | lang:en | layer:interior | p:325

control valve, control valve spring, control valve sleeve
and retaining pin.
7.
In the next bore up, install the manual low control
valve, spring, plug and retaining pin.
8.
In the top right hand bore, install the detent regulator
valve, spring seat, spring and retaining pin.

Inspection
1.
Wash all parts in cleaning solvent and blow out all oil

### Fig. 65M--lnstalling Hub Lip Seal
